info.description: Tenant-scoped graph and DAG API: nodes and edges carrying JSONB, used by AI harnesses as durable memory and as plans they can execute.
info.title: enforcer-graph API

get.description: Discovery endpoint (A2A v1.0 §5.5, docs/A2A_CONTRACT.md §1): what plans this service can start, as A2A skills — one per shipped template (`template:<key>`) plus `import`. Public, no credential. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

post.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 binding of the A2A v1.0 methods this service serves: `SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage` (SSE on this same POST), `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `SubscribeToTask` (SSE), `CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `GetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `ListTaskPushNotificationConfigs`, `DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig` (params `taskId`, plus `id` for Get/Delete and `url`/`token`/`authentication` for Create). v1.0 method names are PascalCase; the pre-v1.0 `message/send` family answers -32601 `MethodNotFoundError`. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.

get.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 GetExtendedAgentCard (spec §9.7): the same card as GET /a2a/agent-card.json, plus `metadata.tenant_id` naming the caller's workspace. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.

post.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 SendMessage (spec §9.1). With no contextId/taskId on the message, starts a new plan — DataPart `{"skill":"template:<key>","slug","name",...}` from a shipped template, or `{"skill":"import","document":<graphimport.Document>}` — and returns the Task for its epoch 1 (TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED). With contextId only, starts the graph's next epoch (gate 3 `reset`, admin). `messageId` is required and deduped per (tenant, account) for 24h: a repeat with the same body replays the same Task (`metadata.replayed: true`); a repeat with a different body is 400 `a2a_message_id_reused`. `configuration.returnImmediately` false (the default) waits up to 30s for the task to settle before answering, `metadata.wait_capped: true` if it did not. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.
post.summary: A2A: send a message (start or advance a plan)

post.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 SendStreamingMessage (spec §9.2): exactly like SendMessage, but the response is an SSE stream of the resulting Task's updates (the same frames SubscribeToTask emits), starting with the Task snapshot. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.
post.summary: A2A: send a message and stream the task

get.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 ListTasks (spec §9.5): epochs of the graphs the caller can see, newest status first. `contextId` narrows to one graph's epoch history; `status` filters by TaskState. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.

REST binding of A2A v1.0 GetTask (spec §9.4): one epoch of a graph, id `<graph_id>.<epoch>`. A graph the caller cannot see, or a malformed id, answers `TaskNotFoundError` — never a bare 403/404 translation — so an outsider cannot distinguish "does not exist" from "exists but is not shared with you". Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.

REST binding of A2A v1.0 ListTaskPushNotificationConfigs (spec §9.6). The caller's own configs on the task; a graph admin (`manage_members`) sees everyone's. Secrets are redacted. Parked configs are listed with `metadata.parked: true`. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.
get.summary: A2A: list a task's push notification configs

post.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig (spec §9.6): registers a webhook for one task (`<graph_id>.<epoch>`). Needs the `stream` verb (viewer) on the graph. `url` must be https, on port 443 or 1024..65535, with no credentials or fragment, and must resolve only to public addresses (checked here and again at every delivery); a refused url is 400 `a2a_push_url_refused` naming the rule. `authentication.scheme` is `Bearer` or `Basic`. `token` is the HMAC key deliveries are signed with (`X-Graph-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(token, t "." body)>`); when absent graph generates one and returns it in this response ONLY — every later read shows `***`. At most 8 live configs per task (the ninth is 400 `a2a_push_limit`); a terminal task answers TaskNotCancelableError. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.
post.summary: A2A: create a task push notification config

get.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 GetTaskPushNotificationConfig (spec §9.6). The caller's own config on a task they can see, or any config for a graph admin; `token` and `authentication.credentials` are redacted to `***`. Another viewer's config is TaskNotFoundError. A parked (dead-lettered) config is returned with `metadata.parked: true` and `metadata.last_error`. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.
get.summary: A2A: get a task push notification config

delete.description: REST binding of A2A v1.0 DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig (spec §9.6). Own config, or any for a graph admin. Idempotent: deleting twice is success. Frames already queued for the config are dropped. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`.
delete.summary: A2A: delete a task push notification config

get.description: Returns the live (non-archived) tenant-wide agent profiles, readable by every accessor of the tenant as /skills are (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §6a). A profile is a routing target: what to run (a local harness subagent type, an A2A card, or a v3 agent). Rows never carry a credential.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: case-insensitive substring match on name or description

post.description: Needs Permissions.TenantManage (the /skills rule, ROUTING_CONTRACT §6b). `runs` is local (local_type), agent (v3_agent_id) or a2a (agent_card_url and v3_agent_id). A v3_agent_id is resolved under the caller's own credential: an agent the caller cannot see, in another tenant, or not active is 422 agent_not_visible; v3 unreachable is 503 agents_unavailable. A name already live in the tenant scope is 409 agent_profile_name_taken.

get.description: An archived or unknown profile, or one scoped to a graph, is 404 agent_profile_not_found.

delete.description: Creator or Permissions.TenantManage. Archives (DELETE never removes the row: route history keeps pointing at it); restore clears it.

patch.description: Any subset of the create body except `runs` (archive and create to change the kind; an unknown key is 400 invalid_body). Creator or Permissions.TenantManage; a member who can see the profile but not write it gets 403 insufficient_scope. Setting v3_agent_id re-resolves the agent as on create.

post.description: Creator or Permissions.TenantManage. A name taken by a live profile meanwhile is 409 agent_profile_name_taken.

Shares the invite's graph with the caller at the invite's role, through the same per-DAG enforcer-v3 share group as POST /graphs/{graphId}/members, and records graph.member_added with the invite id. The token goes in the body, never the path, so it stays out of access logs. An invite never lowers a role: a caller who already holds the invite's role or higher gets shared false and nothing changes, and an accept never takes the caller out of a higher share group. Each account uses an invite once: 410 graph_invite_used when the caller already accepted it, or an admin shared, moved or unshared them while it was live, and they do not hold its role now (ask for a new invite). The caller must be signed in to the invite's workspace: 403 graph_invite_wrong_workspace otherwise, with the workspace id in detail (joining a workspace is enforcer-v3's; join or switch, then accept again). 404 graph_invite_not_found (unknown token, or its graph was archived), 410 graph_invite_expired, 410 graph_invite_revoked. A portal link credential is refused (403 insufficient_scope). 503 groups_unavailable is retried by resending. Shares a rate limit of 10 a minute per account with GET /graph-invites/preview: 429 rate_limited with Retry-After.

get.description: What accepting this invite would join, for a client to show and confirm before POST /graph-invites/accept (the connector's join_plan): the plan's name, the inviter's first name and username, the role it shares at, when it expires and whether the caller already used it, and nothing else. Read-only: nothing is shared or recorded. The token goes in the X-Invite-Token header, never the query string or path, so it stays out of access logs; call it with a plain request keyed on the token, not a cached query hook. graph_name, invited_by_first_name and invited_by_username are text the plan's editors and the inviter chose: show them quoted, as display text, never as proof of identity. The username is unique in the workspace, so it tells two people with one first name apart. Both names come from enforcer-v3's directory and are absent when the inviter has none, the directory cannot be read, or the credential could not read a v3 group member list itself (a fine scope). used is true when the caller already used this link, or an admin shared, moved or unshared them while it was live: accept then answers shared false if they hold its role, else 410 graph_invite_used, so ask for a new link. Every other refusal is accept's, in accept's order: 400 invalid_query with no header, 404 graph_invite_not_found (unknown or malformed token, or the plan was archived), 403 graph_invite_wrong_workspace with the workspace id in detail, 410 graph_invite_revoked, 410 graph_invite_expired; a portal link credential is 403 insufficient_scope. Shares accept's rate limit of 10 a minute per account: 429 rate_limited with Retry-After.
Lists the named graph shapes POST /graphs/from-template can build. Templates ship with the service rather than being tenant data, so every tenant sees the same set.

Returns every graph in the tenant the caller can see — created by them, shared with them (a member row or a group grant), or every graph when their platform role reads tenant-wide (tenant admin, developer). `visibility: tenant` grants nothing on its own: others see a graph only when invited. Each row carries the caller's role on it and can, the verbs that role carries.

post.description: Creates a graph. Mode "dag" enforces acyclicity on every edge write and enables the topology and frontier endpoints; "graph" permits cycles. Lifecycle "terminal" (the default) completes once per epoch; "open" never completes. A lifecycle other than those two is 400 invalid_lifecycle.

Creates the graph, every node and every edge in ONE transaction — all of it lands or none of it does. Building the same shape through POST /nodes/batch then POST /edges/batch is two transactions, so an edge batch rejected for a cycle leaves the nodes behind with no edges. `lifecycle` overrides the template's (terminal or open, else 400 invalid_lifecycle). With `data.promotes_from` naming a graph, that graph must be complete: otherwise 409 source_graph_incomplete, and an OPEN source is never complete ("source graph is open-ended; set lifecycle=terminal to promote from it").
post.summary: Create a graph from a template

post.description: Creates the graph, every node and every edge in ONE transaction. Relations are declared ON the node they leave — `requires` for the scheduling relation, `links` for any other type — so there is no from/to pair to invert. The document is validated exactly like a shipped template before anything is written. `lifecycle` (terminal or open, else 400 invalid_lifecycle) and `loop` (the body of PUT /graphs/{graphId}/loop, with the importer stamped as set_by; a bad key is 400 invalid_body naming it, on=completion with lifecycle open is 400 loop_requires_terminal) are carried onto the graph.
post.summary: Import a graph from a JSON document

post.description: Parses a vault — the shape GET /graphs/{graphId}/vault emits — and builds the graph in ONE transaction. Node keys and relations are read from FRONTMATTER, never from filenames or the prose link section: a filename is sanitised for Obsidian and is lossy, so a filename-keyed import would silently rename nodes. Notes with no frontmatter `key` are skipped rather than refused, so a real vault carrying other notes can be imported.
post.summary: Import a graph from markdown notes

get.description: Returns one graph. A graph the caller cannot see is a 404, never a 403 — a 403 would confirm it exists.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the graph, hiding it from every list and freeing its slug for reuse. Nodes and edges are retained.

patch.description: Edits name, description, visibility, dependency edge type, metadata, the default lease, the judgment `verification_policy` override (`advisory`, `gate` or `gate_human`; an explicit JSON null clears it so the graph inherits the tenant setting), the `approval` policy override (its keys win over the tenant's key by key; an unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the key; an explicit JSON null clears it) or the graph's `mandates` (criteria appended to every run's frozen acceptance list and judged like any criterion: at most 10, each 1..1000 characters after trimming, blank entries dropped; over the caps is 400 invalid_body naming the entry; an explicit JSON null clears them) or the `lifecycle` (`terminal` or `open`, else 400 invalid_lifecycle; open -> terminal on a graph whose live nodes are all done or cancelled emits graph.completed via lifecycle in the same transaction; terminal -> open while the graph has an on=completion loop is 400 loop_requires_terminal; every change emits graph.lifecycle_changed with from and to). The `judgment_budget` ({monthly_tokens, per_epoch_tokens?}: monthly_tokens required, both 1..1e12 tokens; an unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the field; an explicit JSON null clears it) bounds the judgment tokens attributed to this graph per UTC month and per epoch, under the tenant cap, which still applies; a call it cannot fit is skipped with reason graph_budget and the first in a period records graph.budget_exhausted. A PATCH that touches mandates records graph.updated with the mandate count, and one that touches judgment_budget with its monthly_tokens (or cleared). Mode and slug are immutable: changing mode would retroactively invalidate edges the acyclicity check already accepted.

post.description: Advisory only: returns warnings for lines that name no command or quoted literal, use vague phrases ('passes', 'works', 'all passed'), duplicate another line, or exceed 400 characters. Never a 400 for a weak line. Read-only (POST because it takes a body).

get.description: Lists the graph's creator (always admin), its legacy per-account members and its group grants, each grant with kind: share for one of the graph's own per-DAG sharing groups (graph-<graph-id>-viewers|editors|admins; the people it is shared with, managed through /graphs/{graphId}/members) or group for an ordinary enforcer-v3 group grant, each with role and can (the verbs that role carries, from the one capability table), plus my_role/my_can for the caller. On a graph with a validation config, can also carries `judge` (the principal is in the judge pool the config's judges.scope names: owner, graph members, judges.accounts, or a judges.groups slug) and `arbitrate` (owner, tenant admin, or an arbitrators grant), granted by the config, never by a role; the run a principal worked is still refused them. And platform_scope: whether tenant-wide readers and writers exist as a class (a statement, never a list). THIS GET MAKES OUTBOUND CALLS: for each granted group it resolves the members through enforcer-v3's GET /groups/{id}/members under the CALLER's forwarded credential (never a service key), by the group id the grant is bound to. A grant with no bound group id (created before group grants matched by id, and not resolvable since) grants nobody, and reports members.status unknown_group without asking v3. At most 20 groups are resolved per request (the rest are members.status skipped), 4 in flight, 2 s each, so the worst case is about 10 s (12 s with the name lookup below). An upstream 401/403, 404 or timeout is that group's members.status (forbidden, unknown_group, unavailable), never an error here; GRAPH_V3_BASE_URL unset is unconfigured. Member items are what v3 returned after its own redaction (no email for a caller without tenant read), never enriched. accounts is the union of the creator, the legacy members and every resolved group's members: one row per account at its highest role, with via naming each source (creator, member, or share/group with the group's id and slug), built from the same resolution; an account no group listed (creator or legacy member only) is named by ONE further call, enforcer-v3 DirectoryService.BatchGetAccounts under this service's key (cached 60 s, 2 s budget), redacted by the rules v3 applies to a group member list: only for a credential that could read a v3 group member list itself (unscoped or a coarse enforcer scope; a fine graph scope or a portal link gets no names), named only when it is in the caller's tenant, email only for a caller with tenant read, and a failed lookup leaves it unnamed; groups_unresolved is true when that union may be incomplete (a bound grant's members were unavailable, forbidden, unconfigured or skipped, or v3 listed fewer than its total), still 200, and display only: it grants nothing. Each accounts[] row carries kind (human or service, from the same directory read; absent when it could not be read) and, for a service account (an agent), steward: the human answerable for it, read from enforcer-v3's AgentService under the CALLER's credential, so present only when the caller may view that agent. Viewer. An invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found.
get.summary: Who can see and operate on a graph

get.description: Graph-scoped profiles plus the tenant-wide ones, marked inherited: true unless inherited=false. A tenant-wide profile a live graph-scoped profile of the same name overrides is also marked shadowed: true. Needs graph viewer (route_read); an invisible graph is 404.

parameters.name: inherited
parameters.description: false hides the tenant-wide rows (default true)

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: case-insensitive substring match on name or description

post.description: Needs graph editor (manage_profiles). Same body and v3_agent_id rules as the tenant-wide create. A graph-scoped profile may share a tenant-wide profile's name; the graph's wins.

get.description: Needs graph viewer (route_read). A tenant-wide profile id is 404 agent_profile_not_found here: the path named a graph and the row is not that graph's.

delete.description: Needs graph editor (manage_profiles). Archives; routes never point at an archived profile again, history keeps the id.

patch.description: Needs graph editor (manage_profiles). Any subset of the create body except `runs`.

put.description: Graph admin (set_routing). Write-only: sealed with the service keyring (AES-256-GCM, key id as AAD) in a table of its own, 204, and no read of the profile ever returns it. Only runs=agent or a2a profiles hold one; a credential on a local profile, or `remote` on an agent profile, is 400 credential_kind_mismatch. The claim credential is how the bridge authenticates to graph as the agent, never graph's service key. A tenant-wide profile id is 404 here.

delete.description: Graph admin (set_routing). 204 whether or not one was set.

post.description: Needs graph editor (manage_profiles). A name taken by a live profile meanwhile is 409 agent_profile_name_taken.

get.description: How runs routed to this profile fared on THIS graph over the last `days` (1..365, default 30), by node type (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §5c, §6a): a run counts once — rejected when its verification or validation rejected it, else verified when verification verified it or validation accepted it; undecided runs are not counted. Runs are attributed by data.runner_profile, stamped from the route when the run opened. `eligible` marks a line with the 3 decided runs the routing fallback needs. Graph viewer (route_read); a tenant-wide profile id is 404 agent_profile_not_found here, as on every graph-scoped profile route.
get.summary: Get an agent profile's track record

get.description: Lists edges, optionally filtered by type or by either endpoint. Each row carries both endpoints' keys as well as their ids.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: only edges touching this node (either direction)

post.description: Upserts on the triple (from, to, type), so re-asserting a relation is a no-op rather than a duplicate. Endpoints may be given as ids or as node keys. On a dag-mode graph an edge that would close a cycle is refused with 409 edge_would_create_cycle.
Upserts up to 500 edges in ONE transaction — all succeed or none do, so a batch containing a cycle leaves the graph untouched rather than half-written. Endpoints may be ids or keys.

patch.description: Edits weight, data or type. The endpoints are immutable — re-pointing an edge is a delete plus a create. The type may change (a normal write under graph-edges.write, so a dependency that stopped being true can be retired without the destructive delete): the acyclicity trigger re-checks the new shape, the readiness facts follow the change (retyping a dependency edge away releases its dependents), and the previous type is kept in the edge data as retyped_from, retyped_at and retyped_by. A retype onto a type the same endpoints already carry is 409 already_exists.

get.description: Returns the graph's epoch history newest first: one row per epoch (the graph's creation opens epoch 1; each reset closes one and opens the next), with who started and ended it, why it started, when it first completed, the node/run stats taken when it was closed (null on the current epoch), `duration_seconds` (ended_at, or now for the current epoch, minus started_at) and `cycle_seconds` (completed_at minus started_at; null while incomplete). The open epoch carries `current: true`. Viewer on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is a 404.

Returns one row of the graph's epoch history, in the shape listGraphEpochs returns. Viewer on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is 404 graph_not_found, and an epoch the graph never had (or one that is not a positive integer) is 404 epoch_not_found.
get.summary: Get one epoch of a graph

get.description: Returns the entire graph — every node and edge — as structured JSON, capped at 1000 nodes. Pass center and hops to export a subgraph instead.

parameters.name: hops
parameters.description: hop radius when center is given (default 2, max 5)

get.description: Returns previously saved renderings of this graph, newest first. The content digest lets a caller tell whether the graph has changed since an export without downloading it.

post.description: Renders the graph and uploads it to enforcer-files under the CALLER's credential, then records what was produced. Returns both the stored file reference and the rendered content, so one call both saves and returns the workflow file.
post.summary: Render and save a graph export

delete.description: Removes the export record. The file in enforcer-files is not deleted — it is owned by the caller there and may be referenced elsewhere.

get.description: Pages the folder's files as the CALLER may see them (enforcer-files' own redaction applies), under the caller's forwarded credential — never this service's key. An empty page, not an error, when the graph has no folder yet. Viewer.
get.summary: List the files in the graph's shared folder

post.description: Step three of an upload: after PUTting the bytes to upload_url, POST the same file_name here. Forwarded to enforcer-files under the CALLER's credential, so the file is recorded as theirs and then appears in GET /graphs/{id}/files. This is the public complete_url that upload-url returns. Editor.
post.summary: Record a finished upload in the graph's shared folder

post.description: Ensures the graph's folder exists (lazy, idempotent, sharing it with the graph's three DAG groups at read/write/manage) and asks enforcer-files for a presigned upload URL under the CALLER's credential and namespace. PUT the bytes to upload_url, then POST complete_url (this service's POST /graphs/{id}/files/complete) with {"file_name": the same value} to record the upload and get a file_id. Editor.
post.summary: Get a presigned upload URL into the graph's shared folder

get.description: Returns the folder's id, the CALLER's own role on it (read/write/manage/service, resolved by enforcer-files for this request) and its usage. folder_id is null when nothing has been uploaded into this graph yet — no folder is made just by asking. An invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found. Viewer.

Returns the unfinished nodes with no unfinished prerequisite — what an agent can pick up right now. A node with no dependency edges is always in the frontier, which is what makes a fresh task graph start. Only defined on a dag-mode graph. A node whose `not_before` is still in the future is left out of `data` and listed in `waiting` ({node_id, key, not_before}, earliest first) when it would otherwise be runnable, so a harness can tell "not yet" from "blocked by a prerequisite". With rank=1 the same list comes back sorted by priority (blast radius from the graph, risk and effort from the judgment service when the tenant has opted in) with a `rank` object on every node; this GET MAY WRITE A CACHE (nodes.rank) for nodes it judged, and it never fails because the judge did — unavailable or disabled judgment answers 200 with blast-radius ordering and an X-Graph-Rank header (unavailable, token_cap, graph_budget, disabled). Without rank the response is unchanged. `for=me|mine` narrows `data` and `waiting` by assignment (contract §10); absent, every node is listed as before.

parameters.name: rank
parameters.description: 1 or true: rank the frontier by priority and attach rank to each node

parameters.name: for
parameters.description: me: nodes assigned to my account, to one of my groups, or to nobody; mine: only nodes explicitly assigned to me or my groups. Advisory — it narrows what is shown, never what may be claimed. Anything else is 400 invalid_query

X-Graph-Rank.description: present only when ranking was degraded: unavailable, token_cap, graph_budget or disabled

post.description: Takes up to `limit` nodes whose prerequisites are all done, sets each to `running` and opens a run against it — in ONE transaction, with row locks, so two harnesses working the same graph never claim the same node. A `running` node is not in the frontier, so it does not come back until a run finishes. `include=criteria,skills,observations,inputs` returns each node's acceptance list, resolved skills, newest 20 observations and resolved inputs (each data.inputs entry as the upstream node's latest succeeded output with provenance, or absent with a reason; never a failed claim) in the same response, read after the claim commits, so a harness needs one call rather than five. `include=upstream` (depth `upstream_depth`, 1..3, default 1) adds `upstream`: each prerequisite reachable along the dependency edge type, nearest first, with its status, its current-epoch latest succeeded run (outputs, clipped report, verdict, evidence; null when none), newest 10 observations, links and file ids — bounded at 32 KB per prerequisite and 128 KB per card (docs/UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md), and limit must be <= 10 with it. EPOCHS: each card carries `epoch` and `epoch_attempt` (1-based within the epoch, what a retry budget should read); `attempt` stays monotonic across resets, and `failed_attempts` counts failed runs IN THE CURRENT EPOCH only — a contract change for a graph that was reset, identical otherwise. Inputs resolve from the current epoch's runs only (absent `previous_epoch` otherwise) unless a reference ends in `@previous`. Each claimed node carries its work_state (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §17), read through graph_node_work after the claim: `claimed`. LAST_REJECTION (migration 090, no include needed): a card whose node has an earlier attempt this epoch judged `rejected` carries `last_rejection` — that run's id, attempt and stored verdict (state, reason, per-criterion results, checks) plus `rejections` / `max_rejections`, the gate rejections counted this epoch against approval.max_rejections (default 3). A node that reaches the cap is `needs_review`: no claim takes it until a person resolves its rejections_exhausted review item. IDEMPOTENCY-KEY (optional header; printable ASCII, 1–255 characters): a retry with the same key from the same account within 24 hours of the original claim returns the runs that claim opened — the same run ids and nodes — instead of claiming more, with `replayed: true`, header Idempotent-Replayed: true, and each card in its CURRENT state: `run_status` (present only on a replay) says whether the run is still running, or has since succeeded, failed, been abandoned (reclaimed) or cancelled; `lease_expires_at` is the live lease while it runs and its ended_at once it ended. Gate 3 runs first, so a caller who lost the graph gets 404. The same key with a different request (graph, route, node, limit, for, include, upstream_depth or runner) is 422 idempotency_key_reused; a malformed key is 400 invalid_idempotency_key; neither claims anything. A claim that opened nothing (an empty frontier, a refused claim) records nothing, so its retry claims again. Concurrent claims with one key are serialised: one opens runs, the rest replay them. Keys are scoped to (tenant, account); after 24 hours a key claims afresh.
post.summary: Claim runnable nodes from the frontier

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: comma-separated context to return with each node: criteria, skills, observations, inputs, upstream. Read after the claim commits; an unknown value is 400 invalid_query before anything is claimed. upstream (the prerequisites' runs, verdicts, evidence, observations and links, bounded at 128 KB per card) allows limit <= 10.

parameters.name: upstream
parameters.description: slim (default) or full; needs include=upstream. slim: per prerequisite key, title, status, outputs, verdict state+confidence, report excerpt <= 400 chars, evidence_count; full: the whole bundle with evidence

parameters.name: for
parameters.description: me: claim only nodes assigned to my account, to one of my groups, or to nobody; mine: only nodes explicitly assigned to me or my groups. Absent: any node, assigned or not (assignment is advisory). Anything else is 400 invalid_query before anything is claimed

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: optional; printable ASCII, 1–255 characters. A retry with the same key within 24h returns the runs the first claim opened instead of claiming more

parameters.name: X-Graph-Client
parameters.description: optional; the harness, e.g. `enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Recorded on the run (null when absent). The response may carry `warnings` (hooks_inactive, client_outdated); on a graph with client_policy require a missing/outdated client is refused 409 client_attestation_required (claims only)

get.description: Lists explicit per-graph grants made to enforcer-v3 groups. Callers who reach the graph through an account grant, ownership or a tenant role enforcer-v3 grants do not appear here.

post.description: Grants every member of an enforcer-v3 group an explicit role on this graph. The slug is resolved to the group's id in enforcer-v3 under the caller's own credential, and the grant binds to that id: membership is matched by group id, never by slug, so a group created later with the same slug (or deleted and re-created) confers nothing. A slug of the reserved per-DAG share family (graph-<uuid>-viewers|editors|admins) is 400 group_reserved — those are managed by /graphs/{graphId}/members. A slug naming no group in the caller's tenant is 404 group_not_found; enforcer-v3 unreachable is 503 groups_unavailable; a group_id that the slug no longer names is 409 group_id_mismatch. Re-granting an existing slug updates its role and re-binds it to the group the slug names now.
post.summary: Grant a group a role on a graph

delete.description: Revokes the group's explicit grant. Its members may still reach the graph through their own account grant, ownership, or a tenant role enforcer-v3 grants.

patch.summary: Update a graph group grant's role

get.description: Lists this graph's invites, newest first, with their status (active, expired, revoked). Tokens are never returned: only a hash is kept. Graph editor or above (capability invite); a portal link credential is 403 insufficient_scope.

post.description: Makes a link that shares this graph with whoever accepts it (POST /graph-invites/accept), at role viewer or editor (default viewer, as the link is multi-use). It expires after expires_in_hours (default 168, at most 720) and works for any number of people until then or until revoked, once per account. The response is the only place the token appears: only its SHA-256 is stored. url is the portal link, GRAPH_INVITE_URL_BASE + /login#invite=<token> (relative when no base is configured); the token is in the fragment, so it never reaches a server log. Accepting needs an account in this graph's workspace; joining the workspace stays enforcer-v3's. Graph editor or above (capability invite); a portal link credential is 403 insufficient_scope. Records graph.invite_created. The invites a person made are revoked when the graph is unshared from them or they are moved to viewer.

delete.description: Revokes the invite at once; the graph's other invites keep working, and the shares it already made stay (remove those with DELETE /graphs/{graphId}/members/{accountId}). Revoking a revoked invite is a no-op success. 404 graph_invite_not_found when the graph has no invite with this id. Graph editor or above (capability invite); a portal link credential is 403 insufficient_scope. Records graph.invite_revoked.

get.description: The judgment tokens spent on this graph over [from, to): totals plus groups by day (local days in tz, zero-filled), feature (verify, rejudge, align, rank, extract, …) or run — tokens (input + output), input_tokens, output_tokens, calls and estimated_usd (an ESTIMATE: input_tokens × estimate.price_per_mtok_usd / 1,000,000, never an invoice). group_by=run keys are run ids with their node_id; key null holds graph-level calls with no run (rank, align). Only usage recorded since judgment usage was attributed to graphs (migration 068) is here: earlier rows carry no graph and appear only in the tenant's GET /settings/judgment/usage. The graph shares the tenant's monthly cap; the cap block (monthly_token_cap, tokens_used_this_month, resets_at) is included only for a caller with tenant read permission and is null otherwise. When the graph has a judgment_budget (set by PATCH /graphs/{graphId}) the budget block reports it to any viewer: monthly_tokens, used (this UTC month's tokens attributed to the graph), remaining (never below 0) and resets_at (the next 1st, 00:00 UTC), plus per_epoch_tokens, epoch_used and epoch_remaining when it has a per-epoch limit; absent when it has none. A call the budget cannot fit is skipped with reason graph_budget. Parameters as GET /settings/judgment/usage: from/to RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD in tz, at most 400 days, group_by default day, tz default UTC; a bad one is 400 invalid_query. Viewer. An invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found.
get.summary: Get a graph's judgment token usage

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: window start: RFC 3339 instant or YYYY-MM-DD in tz (inclusive)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: window end: RFC 3339 instant (exclusive) or YYYY-MM-DD in tz (that whole day included)

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: IANA time zone for day buckets and date-only bounds (default UTC)

get.description: Lists every link on the graph's nodes, oldest first, paginated on (created_at, id). Filter by system and/or role. Rows only: makes no call to the other services.

put.description: Replaces the graph's loop: a reset the loop worker performs on its own, either when the graph completes (`on: completion`, after `cooldown_seconds`) or every `every_seconds` counted from the epoch's start (`on: schedule`, at least 60), until `max_epochs` (null is unbounded). `force` lets the reset cancel running runs; false skips a busy graph and retries next tick. A loop is RUNS scaled to a graph: it adds no edge and closes no cycle, it starts a new epoch against the same nodes and edges. An unknown key, a value out of range, or `set_by` in the body is 400 invalid_body naming the key; `set_by` is stamped from the caller's account and is the actor on every loop reset. `on: completion` on an open graph is 400 loop_requires_terminal. Admin on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is a 404. Emits graph.loop_changed. The loop is read as the `loop` field of getGraph.

delete.description: Sets the graph's loop to null: manual resets only. Nothing else about the graph changes; the current epoch continues. Admin on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is a 404. Emits graph.loop_changed with `on: none`.

get.description: Lists the accounts this graph is shared with: the members of its per-DAG enforcer-v3 share groups (graph-<graph-id>-viewers|editors|admins, one row per account at its highest role), plus any legacy per-account rows not yet folded into those groups. THIS GET MAKES OUTBOUND CALLS: each share group's members are read through enforcer-v3 under the CALLER's forwarded credential (never a service key), so v3's redaction applies (no email). It never fails because v3 is down: status says whether the v3 part is complete (ok | unavailable | forbidden | unknown_group | unconfigured); anything but ok carries only the legacy rows, and unavailable sets Retry-After. A graph never shared is ok with no items and no call. Callers who reach the graph through ownership, an ordinary group grant or a tenant role enforcer-v3 grants do not appear here (see GET /graphs/{graphId}/access). Viewer.

post.description: Shares this graph with an enforcer-v3 account at a role (a service account, i.e. an agent, is accepted: the acting caller's own credential is forwarded to v3, whose agent fence decides, and a refusal is 403 agent_consent_required, you do not manage that agent, or 403 not_group_member, and changes nothing), by adding the account to the graph's per-DAG v3 share group for that role (graph-<graph-id>-viewers|editors|admins, of the reserved group type `graph`, created on the first share at that role and granted its role on the graph) and removing it from the other two. Re-sharing at another role moves the account; re-sharing at the same role is a no-op success. The account can no longer use this graph's live plan invites, so the share stands until someone sends it a new one. Graph admin only. Every step is idempotent and no step holds a transaction across a call to enforcer-v3, so a 503 groups_unavailable (v3 unreachable, or refusing graph's service key) is retried by sending the same request again. 409 share_group_squatted: the slug is held by a v3 group of another type, and nothing was granted. 404 account_not_found: v3 refused the account (unknown, or in another tenant).
post.summary: Share a graph with an account

delete.description: Removes the account from every one of the graph's share groups (and deletes a legacy per-account row). The groups and their grants stay: a group with no members grants nothing. 404 graph_member_not_found when the graph was not shared with the account. The account may still reach the graph through ownership, an ordinary group grant, or a tenant role enforcer-v3 grants. The plan invites the account created on this graph are revoked, and the graph's live invites no longer let the account back in. Graph admin only; 503 groups_unavailable is retried by resending.

patch.description: Moves the account to the graph's share group for the new role and out of the other two. The account can no longer use this graph's live plan invites, and a move to viewer revokes the plan invites the account created on this graph. 404 graph_member_not_found when the graph is not shared with the account. Graph admin only. Failure codes and retry semantics as addGraphMember.

get.description: Returns the N-hop subgraph around a node — the nodes reachable within `hops` and the edges induced on that set. Depth is capped at 5 and the node count at 1000; the recursive walk terminates even on a cyclic graph. This is the retrieval primitive for grounding an answer in a subgraph.
Lists a graph's nodes, optionally filtered by type or status and searched full-text across key, title, description and string values in the JSONB payload.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: full-text search (websearch syntax: quoted phrases, OR, -exclude)

post.description: Upserts on (graph, key): posting the same key twice updates the existing node rather than creating a duplicate, and JSONB data is shallow-merged into what is already stored. This makes repeated extraction of the same entity safe to retry.
Upserts up to 500 nodes in ONE transaction — all succeed or none do. Same per-node semantics as the single create, so re-sending an extraction batch is safe.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the node. Its edges remain in the database but every traversal (neighborhood, paths, topology, export) skips it. For scheduling it is transparent, never satisfied: its dependents inherit its own prerequisites, so archiving a step never lets a later step run before an earlier one.

patch.description: Edits type, title, description, data, lease_seconds, not_before or the assignee. Set merge_data to shallow-merge the JSONB payload instead of replacing it. `not_before` (RFC 3339) keeps the node off the frontier and unclaimable until that instant; an explicit JSON null clears it, and a past value is accepted and gates nothing. Changing not_before does not clear the node's rank. `assignee_account_id` (a uuid) and `assignee_group_slug` (a group slug) assign the node, advisorily: `for=me|mine` on the frontier and the claim narrow by it, and nothing refuses a claim over it. Each is tri-state — a value sets it, an explicit null clears it, omitting it leaves it — and a real change emits node.assigned; it never clears the rank.

post.description: Claims the named node when its prerequisites are all satisfied, opening a run against it exactly as /frontier/claim does. For an executor that already knows which node it is — a workflow bound to one step — rather than one asking the graph what to do next. Refuses with 409 when the node is not runnable, saying which reason. Takes the same `include` as /frontier/claim, and returns the same card: `epoch`, `epoch_attempt`, and `failed_attempts` counted in the current epoch. Each claimed node carries its work_state (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §17), read through graph_node_work after the claim: `claimed`. LAST_REJECTION (migration 090, no include needed): a card whose node has an earlier attempt this epoch judged `rejected` carries `last_rejection` — that run's id, attempt and stored verdict (state, reason, per-criterion results, checks) plus `rejections` / `max_rejections`, the gate rejections counted this epoch against approval.max_rejections (default 3). A node that reaches the cap is `needs_review`: no claim takes it until a person resolves its rejections_exhausted review item. IDEMPOTENCY-KEY (optional header; printable ASCII, 1–255 characters): a retry with the same key from the same account within 24 hours of the original claim returns the runs that claim opened — the same run ids and nodes — instead of claiming more, with `replayed: true`, header Idempotent-Replayed: true, and each card in its CURRENT state: `run_status` (present only on a replay) says whether the run is still running, or has since succeeded, failed, been abandoned (reclaimed) or cancelled; `lease_expires_at` is the live lease while it runs and its ended_at once it ended. Gate 3 runs first, so a caller who lost the graph gets 404. The same key with a different request (graph, route, node, limit, for, include, upstream_depth or runner) is 422 idempotency_key_reused; a malformed key is 400 invalid_idempotency_key; neither claims anything. A claim that opened nothing (an empty frontier, a refused claim) records nothing, so its retry claims again. Concurrent claims with one key are serialised: one opens runs, the rest replay them. Keys are scoped to (tenant, account); after 24 hours a key claims afresh.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: comma-separated context to return with the node: criteria, skills, observations, inputs, upstream (the prerequisites' runs, verdicts, evidence, observations and links, bounded at 128 KB). An unknown value is 400 invalid_query before anything is claimed.

parameters.name: upstream
parameters.description: slim (default) or full; needs include=upstream. slim: per prerequisite key, title, status, outputs, verdict state+confidence, report excerpt <= 400 chars, evidence_count; full: the whole bundle with evidence

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: optional; printable ASCII, 1–255 characters. A retry with the same key within 24h returns the runs the first claim opened instead of claiming more

parameters.name: X-Graph-Client
parameters.description: optional; the harness, e.g. `enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Recorded on the run (null when absent). The response may carry `warnings` (hooks_inactive, client_outdated); on a graph with client_policy require a missing/outdated client is refused 409 client_attestation_required (claims only)

post.description: Adds a subgraph beneath a node, in ONE transaction. The node is KEPT: its roots inherit the node's prerequisites, and the node itself comes to require the subgraph's leaves — so it becomes a milestone that completes when its children do, and every edge pointing AT it is untouched. A node that is done or has a run in flight cannot be expanded.
post.summary: Expand a node into a subgraph

get.description: Returns the node's links, oldest first (created_at, then id). Rows only: makes no call to the other services.

post.description: Records a link from the node to a thing another service owns: {system, external_type, external_id, role, label?, data?}. The (system, external_type) must name a registered adapter, or it is 400 invalid_body naming the pair; an adapter whose system is not wired in this deployment still accepts links. role is projection, gate or reference. A node cannot hold both a projection and a gate link into one system (409 link_role_conflict); the same (system, external_type, external_id) twice on one node is 409 already_exists. Makes no call to the other service. Emits node.linked, whose metadata never carries external_id.
post.summary: Link a node to an external thing

delete.description: Deletes the link and returns what was removed. A link is never edited: remove it and add it again. Emits node.unlinked, whose metadata never carries external_id.

get.description: Returns the append-only facts recorded against a node, newest first.

post.description: Appends a fact. Idempotent on the body text: re-posting an identical observation returns the existing row with 200 instead of creating a duplicate, so re-processing a source document is safe. When the tenant has opted in to judgment (PUT /settings/judgment), a new body is then judged against the node's most recent observations in ONE call: the same fact restated returns the existing row with 200 and stores nothing (`judgment.decision` = merged); a possible duplicate is stored flagged with `review` = true and `merged_into` set; a distinct fact is stored plainly. Existing observations this one contradicts are recorded in `contradicts`. The judgment runs between two short transactions and never holds a row lock across the network, and adding an observation never fails because the judgment service did — an unavailable judgment stores the row plainly and says so in `judgment.state`.

200.description: an existing row: the same body (exact), or the same fact (judged)

201.description: stored; review=true when judged a possible duplicate

get.description: The route decision for the node's current (epoch, next attempt) (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §3a, §7): which agent profile should do it, which of its skills, how confident and by which method, with `why` composed from the numbers (never model text). `route: null` means no decision yet (the worker has not reached it, or routing is off). A decision of method `none` is a recorded no-route; `reason` says why (below_threshold, tie, all_excluded, no_profiles, jev_unavailable, token_cap, budget). `history=true` adds every decision for the node, newest first, at most 50. A route is advice: it grants nothing. Graph viewer (route_read); an invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found, a node not in it 404 node_not_found.

post.description: With `profile_id` (and optionally `skill_id`): sets the route for the node's current (epoch, next attempt) by hand — method `manual`, decided_by the caller, no confidence (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §5e). The profile must be enabled and visible to the graph (graph-scoped or tenant-wide), else 404 agent_profile_not_found; a profile this attempt excluded because its run was rejected is 409 route_profile_excluded naming the run. With an empty body `{}`: re-routes now — the decision runs in the request (at most 8 s, the editor's call attributed to the graph) and answers 200 with the new route: method `jev`, or the graph's fallback (`arbitrator` leaves method `none` and raises a `route_undecided` review item). If Jev does not answer in time the current decision is superseded and the answer is 202 with the route null; the worker then decides it, with its bounded retry. 409 routing_disabled when the graph has no routing config or enabled false. Graph editor (route_set); an invisible graph is 404, a node not in it 404 node_not_found. Every written decision records node.routed.
post.summary: Set or re-run a node's route

requestBody.description: profile to route to, or {} to re-route

delete.description: Supersedes the current decision with method `none` decided by the caller (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §5e): the worker will NOT route this attempt again (a current none row exists); the next attempt, or POST .../route with {}, will. The node stays claimable, unrouted. Graph editor (route_set); an invisible graph is 404, a node not in it 404 node_not_found. Records node.routed.

get.description: Returns the node's attempts, newest first. This is the loop: three failed attempts and a fourth that succeeded are four rows here, not a cycle in the graph.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: a positive epoch number, or current (the graph's epoch now); absent means every epoch. Anything else is 400 invalid_query

post.description: Opens attempt N+1 against the node and moves the node to "running", exactly as POST /nodes/{nodeId}/claim does: the node must be runnable (every prerequisite done, not already running under a live lease, not done or cancelled), a run whose lease lapsed is closed as abandoned, and the new attempt holds a lease the harness must heartbeat. Refuses with 409 node_not_runnable, saying why. `data` is recorded on the run. The run carries its `epoch`, and this response alone also carries the claim card's `epoch_attempt` and per-epoch `failed_attempts`.

parameters.name: X-Graph-Client
parameters.description: optional; the harness, e.g. `enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Recorded on the run (null when absent). The response may carry `warnings` (hooks_inactive, client_outdated); on a graph with client_policy require a missing/outdated client is refused 409 client_attestation_required (claims only)

patch.description: Closes the attempt and moves the node accordingly: succeeded marks the node done, which can release its dependents into the frontier; failed leaves the node failed so it can be retried as a further attempt. When the tenant has judgment enabled and the node carries `data.acceptance`, a succeeded run is judged AFTER the close commits and the verdict comes back as `verification` (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §2). Under the `gate` policy a rejected verdict moves the node back to failed with `data.failure_reason = verification_rejected`; a judge that cannot answer leaves the run `unverified` for the re-judge worker. Judgment never fails a completion. ATTACH `evidence`: the verdict is what the EVIDENCE shows, not what the report claims, and a succeeded run on a node with criteria that attaches none is `unsupported` — not `verified`. A claim is not evidence for itself. ASYNC JUDGMENT (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §12): this request never calls the judge. A verdict decided without a call (skipped, unsupported, a decisive check row — check rows are evaluated here, with the caller's credential) comes back in this response as before; a verdict that needs the judge comes back as `verification.state = pending` with `judgment_pending_since` set, and the worker writes the real verdict moments later (a `run.judged` event on the stream; GET the run for it). On a validated run the pending call is Jev's vote or the typed-output extraction, and only `judgment_pending_since` is set. DEPRECATED TRANSITION OPT-IN: `?wait=judgment` holds the response until the worker's verdict lands, at most 8 seconds, then answers with whatever is on the run (the verdict, or still pending); it will be removed once the MCP and hooks consumers read the verdict from the stream or the run.

parameters.description: judgment: wait (at most 8s) for the worker's verdict before answering; none (default) answers at once. Deprecated transition opt-in

parameters.description: optional; the harness, e.g. `enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Recorded on the run (null when absent). The response may carry `warnings` (hooks_inactive, client_outdated); on a graph with client_policy require a missing/outdated client is refused 409 client_attestation_required (claims only)

409.description: run_reclaimed | run_already_ended | invalid_transition (a status was named over the node while this run held it, so it cannot enter verifying; detail names the node; nothing was written)

post.description: The run's producer (the account that claimed it) appeals its validation rejection — by the quorum or by an arbitrator's override — within 24 hours of the decision, once per run (docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md §6a). The vote re-opens with fresh seats: n judges drawn at random from the pool, excluding every judge of the first vote (Jev included, so the re-opened vote is the people's alone) and, as always, the run's parties. The node moves from failed back to verifying (dependents wait again) and the verdict is cleared until the new vote decides; a pool smaller than n escalates at once (pool_too_small). Codes: 403 not_run_producer (anyone but the producer), 409 already_appealed (a run is appealed once), 409 appeal_not_allowed (not rejected, the 24 h window has passed, or the node has moved on — a later attempt or a reset; detail says which), 400 invalid_body (note over 4000 characters). A graph the caller cannot see is 404 graph_not_found; a run not in it 404 run_not_found. Returns the re-opened validation.

Sets a flag the run's next heartbeat returns as `state: cancel_requested`. This does NOT close the run, and that is the point: closing it would stop the bookkeeping while the agent kept working, which puts two harnesses on one node by a different route. The harness winds down and reports its own outcome. Its lease keeps being extended while it does, so it is not reclaimed mid-cleanup.

Closes the run, advances its node, and returns the frontier as it stands AFTER that outcome — in one transaction. Identical to PATCH on the run except for the frontier, which otherwise costs a second round trip against a state that may already have moved. The returned nodes are NOT claimed; call /frontier/claim when ready to start. When the tenant has judgment enabled and the node carries `data.acceptance`, a succeeded run is judged after the close commits (by the worker, when the judge must be asked — see below); under the `gate` policy a succeeded run holds the node in `verifying` (its dependents stay blocked, and it is neither claimable nor complete) until the verdict moves it to done, or to failed on a rejection, and the frontier returned is the one AFTER that transition: a rejected node reappears in it for a retry, and a verdict the judge could not give leaves the node verifying for the re-judge worker. Judgment never fails a completion. ATTACH `evidence`: the verdict is what the EVIDENCE shows, not what the report claims, and a succeeded run on a node with criteria that attaches none is `unsupported` — not `verified`. A claim is not evidence for itself. On a graph with a validation config (validation-v1) a succeeded run ALWAYS holds its node in `verifying`, whatever the policy, and `data.validation` comes back in this response: the judges drawn for it and the state (`pending`, or `escalated` with reason `pool_too_small` when fewer judges are eligible than the quorum needs); no Jev verdict is written — the judges decide via castRunVote. ASYNC JUDGMENT (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §12): this request never calls the judge. A verdict decided without a call (skipped, unsupported, a decisive check row — check rows are evaluated here, with the caller's credential) comes back in this response as before; a verdict that needs the judge comes back as `verification.state = pending` with `judgment_pending_since` set, and the worker writes the real verdict moments later (a `run.judged` event on the stream; GET the run for it). On a validated run the pending call is Jev's vote or the typed-output extraction, and only `judgment_pending_since` is set. DEPRECATED TRANSITION OPT-IN: `?wait=judgment` holds the response until the worker's verdict lands, at most 8 seconds, then answers with whatever is on the run (the verdict, or still pending); it will be removed once the MCP and hooks consumers read the verdict from the stream or the run.

The response may carry `warnings` (hooks_inactive, client_outdated); on a graph with client_policy require a missing/outdated client is refused 409 client_attestation_required (claims only)
