post.description: Tells the graph this harness is still alive, pushing the node's lease out by the node's (or graph's) lease seconds. THE RESPONSE IS A CONTROL CHANNEL: `state` is `ok` to keep working, `cancel_requested` if someone asked this work to stop, `reclaimed` if the lease already lapsed and another harness now owns the node (stop — this run's completion will be refused), or `finished` if the run already ended. A long-running agent should heartbeat well inside its lease; a harness that stops heartbeating has its node returned to the frontier rather than stalling the plan forever.

parameters.name: X-Graph-Client
parameters.description: optional; the harness, e.g. `enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Recorded on the run (null when absent). The response may carry `warnings` (hooks_inactive, client_outdated); on a graph with client_policy require a missing/outdated client is refused 409 client_attestation_required (claims only)

post.description: For a run that has ENDED (the worker reported, so the work is done) whose pull request could not land. Stamps the run `outcome: landing_blocked` with `pr_url` and `reason` and HOLDS its node in `needs_review` (never `failed`): no claim takes it, its dependents stay held and its plan stays open. The graph's review queue gets a `landing_blocked` item naming the PR; its `retry` resolution (graph admin) returns the node to `failed`, claimable again. The run must belong to the node's current epoch and the node must be failed, verifying or done (409 invalid_transition otherwise: someone moved it, nothing was written). Recording the same pr_url twice is idempotent. Requires graph editor.
post.summary: Record a landing_blocked outcome on a run

409.description: invalid_transition: the run is still running, already carries another outcome, is from an earlier epoch, or its node is not failed, verifying or done

post.description: Calls the judge with the run's frozen criteria and the evidence so far (the body's `evidence`, else the run's captured evidence) and returns per-criterion probabilities and the score with `interim: true`. It NEVER writes node_runs.verification, a verdict resolution, the node's status or outputs: a progress check is advice. The call is metered like a verdict: it counts against the workspace token cap and the graph's judgment_budget (a refusal comes back 200 with state `skipped` and reason `graph_budget` or `token_cap`). With no evidence nothing is asked (state `unsupported`, reason `no_evidence`); with no acceptance criteria, state `skipped` / `no_acceptance`. Check rows are not evaluated (they need the caller's credential at completion); only judged criteria are scored. Only a RUNNING run can be progress-judged (409 invalid_transition otherwise). Requires graph editor. docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §15.
post.summary: Judge a running run's progress (interim, never a verdict)

requestBody.description: optional evidence and report to judge instead of the run's own

409.description: invalid_transition: the run is not running

get.description: Every verdict the judge gave this run, oldest first. The run's own `verification` is only the latest; a re-judge after an outage, or a curator's re-judge request, adds a row here and never replaces one. Two verdicts with different `question_hash` values were judged on different criteria or evidence.

Every vote cast on this run, oldest first: who voted (an account, never a group seat), accept or reject, and the judge's note. The run's `validation` carries the tally and the state. Viewer on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is 404 graph_not_found, a run not in it (or not on this node) 404 run_not_found.

post.description: Records the caller's `accept` or `reject` on a run in validation and returns the run's validation. Only an ASSIGNED judge may vote — one drawn for this run by account, or a member of a `group:<slug>` seat no one has filled — and never the run's own worker. The quorum is evaluated in the same transaction: `m` accepts move the node from `verifying` to done (dependents released, run.judged, graph.completed if that finished the plan); `n − m + 1` rejects move it to failed (reclaimable for a retry). Codes: 403 not_assigned_judge (can see the graph, holds no open seat), 403 self_judgment_forbidden (the caller worked this run), 409 already_voted, 409 validation_closed (already decided or escalated), 400 invalid_body (vote not accept|reject, note over 4000 characters). A graph the caller cannot see is 404 graph_not_found; a run not in it 404 run_not_found. Records run.voted.

get.description: Returns each attached skill resolved to a concrete version — pinned if pinned, latest otherwise — with its full body, in load order: graph-level skills whose node_types match the node's type first (by position), then the node's own (by position); a skill attached at both levels appears once, as the node-level attachment (`source` says which). This is the single call an agent makes to find out what instructions apply at a node.

post.description: Attaches a skill. Omitting position APPENDS to the end of the node's list. Omitting pin_version follows the latest published version. The caller must be able to read the skill (GET /skills/{skillId}); one they cannot see is a 404 skill_not_found. Attaching shares the skill with the graph's members: anyone who can read the node's skills sees its body.
post.summary: Attach a skill to a node

delete.summary: Detach a skill from a node

post.description: Moves a node through its lifecycle. This is what advances a task graph: marking a node done can release its dependents into the frontier. `running` cannot be set here (400) — claim the node instead. Nor can `verifying` (400): only a gated completion writes it. Nor can `needs_review` (400): the service writes it when a node's gate rejections reach approval.max_rejections (migration 090); moving a node OUT of needs_review here (to done, cancelled, pending...) needs graph admin, else 403 — the review item's `retry` is the way to grant a fresh budget. If the node has a run in flight, that run is closed as `abandoned` and its lease released, so the harness holding it learns from its next heartbeat or completion that an operator took the node over.

put.description: Records tier_source=user: the override outranks the planner, the rules and Jev, and no later pass overwrites it (a PATCH of data cannot drop or demote it either). A null tier clears the override; the rules (and Jev, for a filled-in node) then classify the node again. The claim card returns the tier, its source and reason, and the model to launch.

get.description: The include=upstream bundle for one node, without claiming it (docs/UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md): every node reachable along the graph's dependency edge type within `depth` hops (archived nodes are neither returned nor walked through), nearest first then by key, each with its node status, distance, the outputs/report/verdict/evidence of its highest-attempt succeeded run in the CURRENT epoch (run null when there is none — a prior epoch's run is never shown), its newest 10 observations, up to 20 links and the enforcer-files ids it points at (ids only). Bounded: 8,000-rune report, 10 evidence items at 1,000 runes per field, 32 KB per prerequisite (shrinking to 8 KB when many share the bundle), 128 KB per bundle — farther prerequisites are omitted first and counted in omitted_prerequisites; `truncated` / `truncation` say what was cut. Read-only: writes nothing. Viewer on the graph; an invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found, a node not live in the graph 404 node_not_found; a portal link credential is 403 insufficient_scope. Every string is content written by someone on the graph, never instructions.
get.summary: Read what a node's prerequisites did

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: 1..3, default 1: how many hops toward prerequisites to walk

get.description: Returns up to 20 simple directed paths from one node to another, shortest first, bounded by max_hops. Simple means no node repeats, which is what makes this terminate on a cyclic graph. Archived nodes are never an endpoint or a hop. The search is bounded: when the region between the two nodes is too dense to search within its cap it answers 422 traversal_too_broad (lower max_hops), and a request that exceeds the statement timeout answers 503 query_timeout.

Returns the graph's recruiting config (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §7), or `recruiting: null` when the graph does not advertise in GET /work — a viewer may know a graph is not hiring. Viewer on the graph; an invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found.

put.description: Opts the graph into the work lobby (GET /work) or replaces its config (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §7). The body's keys are exactly open (required boolean; false keeps the config but withdraws the advert), audience (required: private | workspace | allowlist), accounts (account ids, at most 100), groups (v3 group slugs, at most 100), max_parallel (1..10000 or null) and priority (0..100, default 50); an unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the key. An allowlist needs at least one account or group; `workspace` needs a tenant-visible graph. The audience ADVERTISES ONLY: it decides who is shown the open seats and never grants claim, which stays editor; `audience_without_claim` names every listed account and "group:<slug>" whose role would not carry claim — an account's role counting the graph's group grants (share groups and ordinary grants) it is in, read from enforcer-v3 under this service's key (at most 16 granted groups, one 3 s budget); when v3 cannot answer, such an account is named and `groups_unresolved` is true (the warning errs toward naming; the PUT never fails on it). max_parallel is ADVISORY: it caps workers_wanted and nothing refuses a claim at the cap. Graph admin; records graph.recruiting_changed (never the account or group lists).

delete.description: Sets the graph's recruiting config to null: it leaves the work lobby and its audience is forgotten (to pause the advert and keep the audience, PUT with open false). Nothing else changes — the summary still answers and the frontier still claims. Graph admin; an invisible graph is 404. Records graph.recruiting_changed with audience none.

get.description: Renders the whole graph (or a subgraph, via center and hops) as plain text in one of four formats: mermaid (renders natively in Obsidian and GitHub), markdown (an Obsidian note with frontmatter, an embedded mermaid diagram and [[wikilinks]]), text (subject-predicate-object triples, the cheapest form for a language model to read) or dot (Graphviz). Returns text/plain, not JSON.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: mermaid, markdown, text or dot (default mermaid)

parameters.name: hops
parameters.description: hop radius when center is given (default 2, max 5)

post.description: Starts the graph over IN PLACE as epoch N+1: every live node returns to `active` (done, failed, cancelled and verifying ones too; archived nodes stay archived and untouched), and every run, verdict, output, observation, link and edge stays as history under the epoch it belonged to — `attempt` keeps counting, and a claim now opens a run with `epoch` N+1 and `epoch_attempt` 1. A loop is RUNS scaled to a graph: a reset adds no edge. `expected_epoch` is the idempotency guard: when it is not the current epoch the answer is 409 epoch_mismatch with detail "epoch is N"; a client retrying after a lost response sends the same value, gets "epoch is <expected + 1>", and must treat that as done. Omitting it resets every time. With a `running` run or a `verifying` node the answer is 409 graph_busy, detail "running=N verifying=M; pass force to cancel running runs"; `force: true` closes each running run as `cancelled` (its heartbeat then answers `finished` and its `complete` is 409 run_already_ended), and a verifying node's run keeps its validation and votes as history. `reason` (≤ 200 characters, default "manual") goes into the graph.reset event. Unknown keys are 400 invalid_body. Graph admin (the `reset` capability); an editor is 403, a graph the caller cannot see — or an archived one — is 404. The stream delivers graph.reset, which means "refetch everything"; it is not a revocation and closes no stream.
post.summary: Reset a graph into a new epoch

get.description: Every unresolved item judgment produced for this graph, oldest first: an observation stored for review as a possible duplicate (`observation_review`), a contradiction between two observations on one node (`contradiction`), a finished run whose verdict is `rejected` or `unverified` (`verdict_rejected`, `verdict_unverified`), a declared output the judge said is in the evidence but could not pin to one value (`output_uncertain`, id `out:<run_id>:<name>`, with the candidates and the line each appeared on), and a verdict waiting for a person (`verdict_pending`: escalated out of the approval policy's uncertain band, or judged under `gate_human`; under a gate policy its node stays `verifying` until the item is approved or rejected), a gate rejection the judge was not sure of (`low_confidence_rejection`, migration 091: confidence below approval.min_reject_confidence, default 0.6; the node stays `verifying` until a person approves, rejects or re-judges it), and a node whose route waits for a person (`route_undecided`, id `route:<node_id>:<epoch>:<attempt>`: the graph's routing fallback is `arbitrator`, or Jev stayed unavailable past the router's retry bound), and a remote agent's question (`a2a_input_required`, migration 095, id `a2a:<run_id>`: the A2A bridge's remote task is INPUT_REQUIRED or AUTH_REQUIRED; carries `a2a_input` with the state and the question). Items are derived from the rows judgment already writes; nothing here blocks the frontier. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. A graph the caller cannot see is a 404, never a 403.

post.description: Applies one action to one item in ONE tenant transaction and records who did it. Observation review: `keep` (clears the flag), `merge` (archives the duplicate under `into`, default its suspected original), `discard` (archives it). Contradiction: `keep_a` / `keep_b` (archives the other side), `keep_both` (records the pair as reviewed, archives nothing). Verdict: `accept` (the verdict stands; the worker stops re-judging it), `rejudge` (the verdict goes back to unverified and the worker judges the run afresh; the node is not moved; refused with 400 `invalid_action` when the run is not its node's latest attempt, since a superseded verdict can no longer move the node). Pending verdict (`verdict_pending`, requires graph admin): `approve` (the verdict stands as decided by a person; a `verifying` node moves to done and its dependents are released) or `reject` (the verdict becomes `rejected`; the node moves to failed for a retry); both write the verdict and the resolution in one transaction. Output uncertain: `dismiss` (the entry is stamped `dismissed: true` with who and when, and leaves the queue; the value stays null). Route undecided: `approve` with `profile_id` (the node is routed to that profile, method `arbitrator`, decided by the caller; 404 agent_profile_not_found when it is not an enabled profile visible to the graph, 409 route_profile_excluded when a rejected run this epoch excludes it) or `reject` (the node stays claimable, unrouted); on a graph with a validation config this is an arbitrator's call and never a worker of an earlier attempt's (self_judgment_forbidden), else graph editor. Low-confidence rejection (`low_confidence_rejection`): `approve` (the node moves to done), `reject` (the node moves to failed and the rejection counts toward max_rejections) or `rejudge`. Rejections exhausted (migration 090; the node's gate rejections this epoch reached approval.max_rejections and it is `needs_review`, claimable by no one): `retry` (requires graph admin; the node returns to `failed` with a fresh budget of max_rejections and is claimable again) or `approve` (requires graph admin; the latest rejected verdict is re-applied as verified by a person, the node moves to done and the counter restarts). A `verdict_rejected` item likewise takes `approve` (graph admin; same effect, refused on a superseded attempt). To abandon the work instead, PATCH the node's status to done or cancelled (also graph admin from needs_review). A2A input required (graph editor): `reply` with `text` (the bridge sends it as a message on the remote task and the run goes on) or `fail` (the bridge cancels the remote task and fails the run). A second resolve of the same item is 409 `already_resolved`; an action outside the item's kind is 400 `invalid_action`; `merge` with an `into` that is not an observation on the same node is 400 `invalid_body`. Every resolution emits one activity event with the caller as actor. Never calls the judgment service. Verdict review on an `unverified` run that HOLDS its node in `verifying` (gate): `approve` writes the verdict `verified` and moves the node to done, `reject` writes `rejected` and moves it to failed, `rejudge` asks the worker again; `accept` is refused there (400 invalid_action) because it would record a resolution and leave the node held for good. On an unverified run whose node is not held, `approve`/`reject` are refused and `accept` / `rejudge` apply. A prior `accept` on a held run is not final: the item may be resolved again with an action that releases. Override (validation-v1 §6a; item `run:<run_id>` of a run whose validation the vote DECIDED, accepted or rejected): an arbitrator — owner, tenant admin or an arbitrators grant, never a party to the run (self_judgment_forbidden) — overturns the decision with a required `note` (400 missing_field otherwise): accepted becomes rejected (verdict rejected, reason overridden_by_arbitrator; the node moves to failed) and rejected becomes accepted (verdict verified; the node moves to done); both verdicts and the run's validation carry decided_by `arbitrator`, and the validation records `override` {by, at, note, from}. A pending or escalated validation is 409 validation_not_decided (an escalated run takes approve / reject); a superseded attempt is 400 invalid_action.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: item id from the queue (obs:…, pair:…:…, run:…, out:…:…, route:…:…:…, held:…:…, a2a:…)

get.description: Returns the graph's routing config (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §2c, §7) with its defaults applied, or `routing: null` when routing is off, plus `profiles_visible`: the enabled, live agent profiles a route on this graph may choose (graph-scoped plus tenant-wide not shadowed by name). Routing is ON only when enabled is true AND profiles_visible > 0. Graph viewer (route_read); an invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found.

put.description: Turns routing on (or off with enabled false) or replaces its config (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §2c, §7). Keys: enabled (required boolean), threshold (0.50..0.99, default 0.65), margin (0..0.5, default 0.10: the top profile must beat the runner-up by this or it is a tie), fallback (track_record | arbitrator | none, default track_record: what decides below the threshold or on a tie), upstream_depth (1..3, default 1), max_profiles (1..16, default 16); an unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the key. The stored config has the defaults filled in. With routing on, the worker decides a route for every claimable node (a due-scan on its tick; a claim never waits for it); `arbitrator` currently records method none like `none`. Graph admin (set_routing); an invisible graph is 404. Records graph.routing_changed.

delete.description: Sets the graph's routing config to null (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §7): the worker stops deciding routes for it. Route rows already written stay as history. Graph admin (set_routing); an invisible graph is 404. Records graph.routing_changed with enabled false.

get.description: Returns execution attempts across the whole graph, newest first — the graph's execution history. Filter by `status` and `runner` together (`?status=running&runner=worker-3`) to find a restarted harness's own in-flight work: without it, a harness that crashes and comes back has no way to learn which nodes it still holds a lease on.

parameters.name: runner
parameters.description: exact runner, as recorded on the run's data at claim time

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: a positive epoch number, or current (the graph's epoch now); absent means every epoch. Anything else is 400 invalid_query

get.description: Returns each skill attached at graph level (migration 092), resolved to a concrete version — pinned if pinned, latest otherwise — with its node_types filter (null = every type), in load order (position, then skill id). A node's resolved list (GET .../nodes/{nodeId}/skills, the claim card) puts the ones matching its type first, then its own.

post.description: Attaches a skill to every node of the graph whose type is in node_types (omitted or null = every type), loaded before each node's own skills (migration 092). Omitting position APPENDS; omitting pin_version follows the latest published version. Re-attaching the same skill replaces its node_types, pin and config and keeps its position unless one is given. The caller must be able to read the skill; one they cannot see is 404 skill_not_found. An empty node_types list is 400 invalid_body. Graph editor.
post.summary: Attach a skill to a graph

delete.description: Removes a graph-level attachment (migration 092). Node-level attachments of the same skill are untouched. Graph editor; an attachment that does not exist is 404 graph_skill_not_found.
delete.summary: Detach a skill from a graph

get.description: Per-node wait (ready_at to started_at), run time and token usage, plus graph totals, so dispatch latency and cost are visible without a transcript scrape. Every figure is a trigger-maintained derived fact (migration 088), read in one snapshot. `totals.runs_by_client` and `totals.runs_without_client` (migration 089) count the graph's runs by the X-Graph-Client they reported and the runs that reported none, so a harness running without the plugin's hooks is visible. Usage is OPTIONAL on a run: totals are absent (null), never 0, when no run reported any, and `runs_without_usage` says how many runs reported nothing - a token total beside a non-zero count is a lower bound. `nodes` pages the live nodes (limit default 50, max 200); `totals` always covers the whole graph. Read-only. Viewer on the graph; an invisible graph is 404.
get.summary: Get a graph's timing and usage stats

get.description: Server-Sent Events: one frame per activity row as it commits, plus `ready`, `reset`, `closed` and a keepalive comment (docs/STREAM_CONTRACT.md). Each event means "this graph changed, refetch"; resume with `Last-Event-ID`. Any credential that can read the graph can stream it; the fine scope is `enforcer:graph-stream.read`, and a credential holding only `enforcer:graph-runs.write` cannot stream. Not a generated query hook: the body never ends.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: resume cursor: the id of the last event received

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: alias for Last-Event-ID; the header wins

get.description: One DAG's work card, computed in ONE SQL statement so every number is one snapshot (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §4): the roll-up `state` (complete | recruiting | working | waiting | stalled), live nodes by derived `work_state` and by `status` (every status, zero when absent), progress, demand (`workers_wanted` shaped by the graph's advisory `recruiting.max_parallel`, `judges_wanted` from open validation seats, the open work seats by node type, skill and assignee group, the next `opens_at`), leases (live, expiring within `expiring_within` seconds, expired = reclaimable, missing = running with no lease, which must be 0), derived worker presence (distinct accounts holding a live lease — claimed and alive, not online), pending validations, failures this epoch, the remaining critical path (`remaining`, `bounded`, and `node_ids` — one longest chain of unfinished live nodes in path order, root first, exactly `remaining` long) and run throughput. Read-only: nothing here ranks, caches or meters. Poll at 5 s or slower; the server does not cache. Viewer on the graph; an invisible graph is 404 graph_not_found; a graph-mode graph is 409 graph_not_acyclic (the work states are defined by the frontier). `expiring_within` outside 0..86400 is 400 invalid_query.

parameters.name: expiring_within
parameters.description: lease window in seconds for leases.expiring_within (default 300, max 86400)

get.description: Returns nodes in execution order — ascending dependency level, where level 0 has no unmet prerequisite. Only defined on a dag-mode graph; a cyclic graph returns 409 graph_not_acyclic rather than an arbitrary order that would read like a real answer.

Returns the graph's validation-v1 config (docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md §3), or `validation: null` when validation is off and `verification_policy` / `approval` apply exactly as before. Viewer on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is 404 graph_not_found.

put.description: Opts the graph into validation-v1 (docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md §3) or replaces its config. From then on every run that ends `succeeded` holds its node in `verifying` (dependents wait, whatever `verification_policy` says) while `quorum.n` judges drawn AT RANDOM from the pool — never the run's own worker — vote; `quorum.m` accepts release the node, `n − m + 1` rejects fail it for a retry. The config is snapshotted onto each run as it enters validation, so a change here never alters a vote in flight. Validation: the body's keys are exactly quorum {m, n} (1 ≤ n ≤ 15, ceil(n/2) ≤ m ≤ n), judges {scope private|workspace|allowlist|none, accounts (account ids), groups (v3 group slugs)}, jev, arbitrators {accounts, groups} and deadline_seconds (60..2592000, default 86400); an unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the key. Every judges.groups / arbitrators.groups slug must name a live enforcer-v3 group in the caller's tenant (resolved under the caller's own credential): the config binds each slug to that group's id, and a group seat is filled — and an arbitrator group matched — only by members of THAT group, never by a group created later with the same slug. A slug naming no group is 404 group_not_found; enforcer-v3 unreachable is 503 groups_unavailable; a slug already bound to a different group (deleted and re-created) is 409 group_id_mismatch unless named in `rebind`. `workspace` needs a tenant-visible graph. With `jev: true` Jev holds one of the n seats: after the completion commits (or later, from the re-judge worker, when the judge was unavailable or the token cap was reached) it votes through the graph's approval policy — accept when the aggregate is verified, reject when rejected or unsupported, undecided (counts as neither) when it stays inside the uncertain band; an undecided Jev escalates `jev_undecided` once the seats still uncast can reach neither m accepts nor n − m + 1 rejects. Scope `none` (Jev alone) requires `jev: true` and n = 1. Graph admin; records graph.validation_changed.

parameters.name: rebind
parameters.description: group slugs (comma-separated) to re-bind to the group each names now

delete.description: Clears the graph's validation config: later completions follow `verification_policy` and `approval` again. Runs already in validation keep their snapshot and are still decided by their judges (or escalate). Idempotent. Graph admin; records graph.validation_changed.

get.description: Runs in this graph whose validation is `pending`, where the caller holds an assigned seat no one has filled yet — their own account, or a `group:<slug>` seat for a group they are in — and has not voted, oldest first. The caller's own runs (they were the worker) are never listed: they may not judge them. Viewer on the graph; a graph the caller cannot see is 404 graph_not_found.
get.summary: List runs waiting on my vote

get.description: Returns one markdown note per node plus an index, each with YAML frontmatter and [[wikilinks]] to its neighbours. Written into a vault, Obsidian's own graph view reconstructs the graph from those links — which a single-file export cannot do, since that view builds its graph from links BETWEEN notes.
get.summary: Export a graph as an Obsidian vault

parameters.name: hops
parameters.description: hop radius when center is given (default 2, max 5)

get.description: The same folder GET /vault returns as JSON, packed so it can be extracted straight into a vault: `curl -OJ` then `tar -xzf`, and point Obsidian at the folder. One note per node with [[wikilinks]], so Obsidian's graph view reconstructs the shape. Returns the archive bytes, not an envelope — the only endpoint here that does.
get.summary: Download a graph as an Obsidian vault (.tar.gz)

parameters.name: hops
parameters.description: hop radius when center is given (default 2, max 5)

get.description: Filters, sorts, groups and aggregates nodes across every graph the caller can see (docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §6). A graph the caller cannot see — including one named in graph_id — is silently excluded: the result is smaller, never a 403 or 404. Archived graphs are never included. Each item carries work_state, reclaimable and opens_at exactly as getNode reports them (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §2; absent on an archived node and on a graph-mode graph's), and, on a running node, claimed_by, runner and run_id (its running run's created_by, data.runner and id). `work_state` filters on the same derived state, computed through graph_node_work. Without group_by (and without a non-count agg) the data is {items, total, limit, offset} plus, when the request has no offset and a following page exists, next — the opaque cursor to pass back as after (keyset paging: exact under concurrent writes, and a deep page costs what page one does); with either it is {groups, total_groups, limit, offset}, where each group carries key, count, aggs, skipped and (for output aggregates) currency. Read-only. `where` is a JSON array of at most 16 predicates, at most 4 KiB: [{"path":"data.priority","op":"gte","value":3}] — path ^(data|output)(\.[a-z0-9_]+){1,8}$, op one of eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, contains, exists, missing, prefix, ilike; every value is bound, never interpolated. An unknown parameter is 400.

get.description: Returns the service's public status without authentication — the pattern for webhooks and public probes.

Filters, sorts, groups and aggregates runs across every graph the caller can see (docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §7) — cycle time by epoch is one GET: ?node_key=reconcile&group_by=epoch,claimer&agg=avg:duration,p95:duration. Items are runs as listGraphRuns returns them (bodies included) plus node {id, key, type}; groups never carry a run body. Without group_by (and without a non-count agg) the data is {items, total, limit, offset} plus, when the request has no offset and a following page exists, next — the opaque cursor to pass back as after; otherwise {groups, total_groups, limit, offset}. Read-only. An unknown parameter is 400.

parameters.description: csv of node ids, at most 50 (more is 422)

parameters.name: on_behalf_of
parameters.description: me or an account uuid: runs done FOR that human — by an agent they steward, or a program acting as them

parameters.description: current (default), all, or a csv of epoch numbers; group_by=epoch defaults to all

parameters.name: verdict
parameters.description: csv of verified, rejected, unverified, unsupported, skipped, pending, none — this run's verdict

parameters.name: min_duration_seconds
parameters.description: duration at least this (running runs excluded)

parameters.name: max_duration_seconds

parameters.name: has_evidence

parameters.name: include_archived

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: IANA time zone for time buckets (default UTC)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: rows (or groups) to skip; not with after

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: opaque keyset cursor: the previous page's next, passed back unchanged with the same sort (at most 1024 bytes). Not with offset, group_by or a non-count agg (400 invalid_query); malformed, or issued for another sort, is 400 invalid_cursor. Prefer it to offset for every page past the first

get.description: The tenant's opt-in to Jev-backed judgment: whether it is on, which model, the verification policy (advisory, gate, or gate_human — every gate verdict waits for a person) and `verification_policy_source` (`tenant` when this tenant chose it, `default` when it never did and the platform default applies — gate since migration 090: a rejected run fails its node and holds its dependents), dedupe and contradiction toggles, the monthly token cap and how much of it is used, the tenant's mandates (criteria appended to every run's frozen acceptance list and judged like any criterion), and the approval policy (samples, aggregate, pass rule, uncertain band, escalation, high stakes; `{}` is every default). A tenant that has never opted in reads the defaults with enabled=false. The tenant's own key is never returned; has_tenant_key says whether one is set.

put.description: Replaces the whole configuration (this is not a patch). verification_policy is optional: omitted or null stores no choice, and the platform default (gate) applies to every graph without its own override. tenant_key is write-only: omit it to keep the current key, send "" to clear it and fall back to the platform key, or send a key to replace it — it is stored as ciphertext and never returned. model defaults to jev-latest and is stored as the versioned id it resolves to, so a tenant's tuned thresholds never drift under them. mandates (at most 10, each 1..1000 characters after trimming, blank entries dropped) replaces the tenant's mandates; omit it to keep them, send [] to clear them; over the caps is 400 invalid_body naming the entry. approval replaces the approval policy (samples "1"|"adaptive"|"3"|"5", aggregate median|all_must_pass, pass {noul, score}, uncertain_band [lo, hi], escalate_to none|human|claude-sonnet-5|claude-opus-5-5, high_stakes {risk_min, blast_min, then}); omit it (or send null) to keep it, send {} for every default; an unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the key. verification_policy gate_human holds every gated node for a person's approve or reject in the review queue. Emits judgment.settings_changed with the mandate count. Requires tenant management permission.

get.description: Where the tenant's judgment tokens went over [from, to): totals plus groups by day (local days in tz, zero-filled), feature (verify, rejudge, align, rank, extract, …), graph, or model — tokens (input + output, what the monthly cap counts), input_tokens, output_tokens, calls, and estimated_usd. estimated_usd is an ESTIMATE: input_tokens × estimate.price_per_mtok_usd / 1,000,000 at the price this service is configured with (GRAPH_JEV_PRICE_PER_MTOK_USD, default 0.042), never an invoice. Rows recorded before usage was attributed to graphs (migration 068) have no graph: they appear under group key null and in totals.unattributed_tokens, and every total still includes them. Also returns the cap block — monthly_token_cap, tokens_used_this_month (the figure GET /settings/judgment reports) and resets_at (the next 1st, 00:00 UTC). from and to are RFC 3339 instants or YYYY-MM-DD dates in tz (a date `to` includes that whole day); from defaults to 00:00 of the day 29 days before today in tz, to to now; to - from is at most 400 days; group_by defaults to day, tz to UTC (an IANA zone name). A bad parameter is 400 invalid_query naming it. Requires tenant read permission, as GET /settings/judgment does.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: window start: RFC 3339 instant or YYYY-MM-DD in tz (inclusive)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: window end: RFC 3339 instant (exclusive) or YYYY-MM-DD in tz (that whole day included)

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: IANA time zone for day buckets and date-only bounds (default UTC)

get.description: Returns the latest non-archived version of every skill in the tenant. Use the versions endpoint to see a skill's history.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: case-insensitive substring match on name or description

post.description: Publishes version 1. Use the versions endpoint to publish subsequent versions; a published body is never edited in place.

delete.description: Retires all versions of the slug. Existing attachments keep resolving, so archiving hides a skill from listings without breaking graphs that already reference it.

get.description: Returns every published version of the skill's slug, newest first. Attachments can pin any of them.

post.description: Creates version N+1 of this skill's slug. Nodes attached without a pinned version pick it up immediately; nodes that pinned a version keep the one they pinned.

get.description: Echoes the federated identity (account, tenant, role) resolved by enforcer-v3 for the caller's credential.

The work lobby (docs/WORK_LOBBY_CONTRACT.md §8): every graph the caller can see that advertises open seats to it — a live dag graph with `recruiting.open`, whose audience includes the caller — and has demand. A graph the caller cannot see, or whose audience excludes it, is simply absent (never a 403); so is one with no open seat for this `kind`. Each row carries the roll-up state, the caller's role and `my_can`, `workers_wanted` (open work seats capped by the graph's ADVISORY `max_parallel` less its live leases) and `judges_wanted` (open validation seats, Jev's excluded), the seats broken down by node type, skill and assignee group, and where to act. The audience ADVERTISES ONLY: a row may list work the caller cannot claim — check `my_can` for `claim` (editor). PULL, not dispatch: nothing is reserved, and two workers reading one row race the atomic claim as today. `kind`: any (default: work or validation seats), work, validation. `for`: me (seats assigned to my account, one of my groups, or nobody; for validation, my own or my groups' seats) or mine (explicitly mine only). `type`, `skill`, `group` (comma-separated, exact) narrow the counted work seats. Ordered by demand, then priority. Poll at 10 s or slower: each row is one frontier evaluation. A statement past the query timeout is 503 query_timeout. Anything else malformed is 400 invalid_query.

parameters.name: for
parameters.description: me or mine: count only seats assigned to the caller (me also counts unassigned work seats)

blast_min.description: BlastMin, a non-negative integer: a blast radius at or above it is high stakes.

risk_min.description: RiskMin in [0,1]: the node's stored rank.risk at or above it is high stakes.

alpha.description:
Alpha, ceil((k+1)/2)..k (a strict majority): how many of a round's
samples must agree for the round to count. Default 2.

beta.description: Beta, 1..5: consecutive agreeing rounds that decide. Default 2.

max_rounds.description:
MaxRounds, beta..20: rounds before an undecided run escalates per
escalate_to. Default 8.

aggregate.description:
Aggregate: median (per criterion and for the score) or all_must_pass
(every sample passes the pass rule). Default median.

escalate_to.description:
EscalateTo is who is asked when the aggregate is still uncertain. The
claude-* names fall back to human (escalated_fallback on the verdict).
Default human.

high_stakes.description: HighStakes switches to `then` for a risky or far-reaching node.

max_rejections.description:
MaxRejections, 1..20: gate rejections a node may take in one epoch
before it needs review (not claimable; a person resolves it). Default 3.

min_reject_confidence.description:
MinRejectConfidence, 0..1: under gate, a rejection whose confidence is
below this does not fail the node; a person decides (review item
low_confidence_rejection). Default 0.6; 0 restores today's behaviour.

pass.description: Pass is the pass rule. Default {noul: 0.70, score: 1.50}.

samples.description:
Samples: "1" one call; "3"/"5" that many; "adaptive" one call, and four
more only when a value lands inside uncertain_band; "snowball" rounds
of k calls until one outcome wins beta rounds in a row (see snowball).
Default adaptive.

snowball.description:
Snowball is the parameters samples "snowball" uses (also when
high_stakes.then selects it). Merged as one unit; omitted keys take
the defaults {k: 3, alpha: 2, beta: 2, max_rounds: 8}.

uncertain_band.description:
UncertainBand is [lo, hi], both in [0,1], lo < hi. A criterion noul or
score/2 inside it is uncertain. Default [0.55, 0.85].

error.description:
Error is set when the check could not be evaluated; Passed is then
false and the verdict is `unverified` with reason `check_error`.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle and Loop are what the template or document declared
(docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §1, §4); Loop is null when none.

detail.description:
Detail is optional human-readable context for the SAME machine code —
never a second code, and never something a client branches on. It exists
because a caller whose document was refused needs to know which node named
an unknown key; `invalid_body` alone is not actionable.

omitempty, so every response that does not set it is byte-identical to
before this field existed. The platform already uses `detail` this way:
authz.RequireBillingWritable echoes the tenant's billing status beside
billing_restricted.

mandate.description:
Mandate is "graph" or "tenant" on a row the tenant or graph imposed
(migration 040), absent on the node's own criterion. Set by the caller
that knows the frozen rows (runs.BuildVerdict); this package only asks.

cmd.description:
command: what ran, what it exited with, what it printed.

Exit is a POINTER because it is often unknowable. A Claude Code Bash
tool_response carries no exit field: success arrives as an object
(stdout, stderr, interrupted...) and failure arrives as a plain string,
"Error: Exit code N\n<output>", which is the only place the number is
written down. A capture hook that cannot parse it must still be able to
attach the output — dropping the item would weaken the verdict in
exactly the case that matters most, a command that failed.

file.description:
File is an enforcer-files file_id holding the WHOLE of what Output
holds a clip of (adapter-files). A harness uploads a command output
longer than the clip under the user's own credential and records the id
here, so the middle the 30/70 clip elides is one click away for the
person reading the verdict. It is a uuid or it is dropped. Nothing in
this service downloads it during verification: the judge sees the clip
and a line saying the clip is not the whole (VerifyEvidenceQuestions).

file_bytes.description:
FileBytes is the stored file's size as the uploader measured it, quoted
in that line. Optional; kept only beside a file, and never negative.

kind.description:
Kind is command | file | artifact | note. An unrecognised kind is kept
and shown to the judge rather than dropped — a harness inventing a
kind is still telling us something, and silently discarding evidence
would turn a report that tried into one that did not.

path.description: file: a path and the part of it that matters.

text.description: note: prose. Accepted, and deliberately weak — see EvidenceQuestions.

candidates.description:
Candidates are at most OutputCardCandidates canonical values, only when
Value is null and the judge said a value is present: the review card.

confidence.description:
Confidence is the choice question's (extracted) or the grounded
noul's (declared). Absent when no answer was read.

dismissed.description: Dismissed is set by a curator's `dismiss`; the entry leaves the queue.

evidence_index.description:
EvidenceIndex indexes node_runs.evidence for the chosen candidate;
null for declared.

present.description: Present is P(a value is in evidence at all); null for declared.

reason.description:
Reason is `unavailable` when this output's answers were missing or
mistyped, `overflow` when it did not fit the call. The verdict is
unaffected either way.

resolved_by.description: ResolvedBy and ResolvedAt stamp the curator's resolution.

value.description: Value is the canonical value, or null when it was not accepted.

monthly_tokens.description:
MonthlyTokens bounds the graph's spend per UTC calendar month.
Required, 1..1e12.

per_epoch_tokens.description:
PerEpochTokens, when set, also bounds the spend since the graph's
current epoch started (a reset starts a new epoch). 1..1e12.

epoch.description: Epoch is the graph's current epoch, which per_epoch_tokens counts.

per_epoch_tokens.description:
PerEpochTokens and the two fields after it are present only when the
budget has a per-epoch limit: the graph's tokens since its current
epoch started, and what is left of that limit (never below 0).

remaining.description: Remaining is monthly_tokens - used, never below 0.

resets_at.description: ResetsAt is the next 1st of the month, 00:00 UTC.

used.description: Used is the graph's tokens (input + output) this UTC month.

archived_at.description:
Review resolution (migration 020, contract §10). ArchivedAt is set by
merge/discard (or the losing side of a contradiction pair): the row is
out of every read but never deleted. Resolution records how a curator
closed this row's review item; ResolvedContradictions lists the older
observations whose contradiction with this row has been resolved.

contradicts.description:
Contradicts lists existing observations on the same node this one
contradicts (P >= judgment.AlignContradictionMin at judgment time). Not a
foreign key: the record that a contradiction was found outlives the row.

review.description:
Review marks a judged POSSIBLE duplicate of MergedInto: stored, flagged
for a human. A row the judgment called the same fact is never stored, so
MergedInto is only ever set together with Review (migration 014 CHECK).

support.description:
Support is grounded | asserted | decision | unjudged (migration 023):
whether this fact is a measurement, a hunch, a recorded choice, or
unjudged. A LABEL, never a gate — an asserted row is stored exactly as
before. It travels on every read so a later agent can tell a hunch from a
measurement instead of treating both as established, which is the whole
point: observations are re-served as context on every claim.

email.description: Email is present only when v3 sent it — for a caller holding AdminRead.

cooldown_seconds.description:
CooldownSeconds is the wait after completion before the reset
(completion only; 0..315360000; absent means 0).

every_seconds.description:
EverySeconds is the schedule interval, counted from the epoch's start
(schedule only; 60..315360000).

force.description:
Force: whether a loop reset cancels running runs. False skips a busy
graph and retries next tick.

max_epochs.description: MaxEpochs stops the loop once epoch >= max_epochs; null is unbounded.

on.description: On is what triggers a reset: the graph completing, or a fixed interval.

source.description:
Source: reported (the provider's own counters) or estimated (the
harness's guess). Defaults to reported when omitted.

pinned_version.description:
PinnedVersion nil means "follow the latest published version". A value
pins, which is what makes a graph an agent walks reproducible instead of
drifting when someone publishes a new version underneath it.

position.description:
Position is the load order and is therefore part of the contract, not
decoration.

source.description:
Source says where the attachment came from on a node's resolved list:
"graph" (a graph-level skill matching the node's type, migration 092)
or "node" (attached to this node). Graph-level skills load first.

description.description:
Description is how an agent decides whether to load the body at all, so it
is required rather than optional.
description.example: Run build, vet and tests before calling anything done.

previous_judges.description:
PreviousJudges are the first vote's judges (and "jev" when Jev sat):
none of them holds a seat in the re-opened vote.

previous_tally.description: PreviousTally is the first vote's tally.

rejected_at.description: RejectedAt is when the appealed rejection was decided.

arbitrators.description:
Arbitrators are explicit grants IN ADDITION to the graph owner and
tenant admins, who always arbitrate.

deadline_seconds.description:
DeadlineSeconds: a run still undecided this long after it entered
validation escalates (reason `deadline`). 60..2592000; absent means
86400.

jev.description:
Jev: Jev is one of the n judges, its vote the graph's approval
policy's aggregate (accept, reject, or undecided inside the band).

reason.description:
Reason is why the last attempt cast nothing: unavailable, key_unusable,
token_cap, check_error.

verdict_id.description:
VerdictID is the run_verdicts row (applied = false) holding Jev's
aggregate — the approval policy's verdict this vote was read from.

vote.description: Vote is accept, reject or undecided; absent while uncast.

groups.description:
Groups are v3 group SLUGS naming live groups in the caller's tenant.
Each is BOUND to its v3 group id when the config is written (063), and
is one seat in the draw, filled by whichever member of THAT group (by
id) votes first — never by a later group that took the slug.

scope.description:
Scope: private (owner + accounts/groups), workspace (owner + graph
members + accounts/groups; the graph must be tenant-visible),
allowlist (only accounts/groups; at least one), none (no people;
Jev alone: requires jev and n = 1).

from.description: From is the quorum's decision the arbitrator overturned.

m.description: M: how many must agree. ceil(n/2) <= m <= n, so a minority never decides.

n.description: N: judges assigned to each run. 1..15.

appeal.description:
Appeal is set once the run's producer appealed a rejection (§6a): the
vote was re-opened with fresh seats, excluding PreviousJudges.

assigned.description:
Assigned are the judges drawn at random for this run: account ids and
"group:<slug>" seats (any member of that group may fill one).

config.description:
Config is the graph's config AS IT WAS when this run entered
validation: editing the graph's config never changes a vote in flight.

deadline_at.description:
DeadlineAt is when a still-pending run escalates for `deadline`:
opened_at + config.deadline_seconds. Computed, never stored (045's
validation_deadline_at is the stored rule).

decided_by.description:
DecidedBy is quorum on a vote's decision, arbitrator once an escalated
run was approved or rejected; null while pending or escalated.

escalated_at.description: EscalatedAt is when the run escalated; absent otherwise.

filled.description:
Filled maps each seat that has voted to the account that filled it,
so one group seat is filled once.

jev.description:
Jev is Jev's seat, present once Jev was asked: the vote it cast (or
the attempts that could not cast one). Absent when jev is false.

override.description:
Override is set once an arbitrator overturned the quorum's decision
(§6a): who, when, the note and the decision overturned. DecidedBy is
then arbitrator.

reason.description:
Reason is set when escalated: pool_too_small (fewer eligible judges
than n when validation opened), deadline, or jev_undecided (Jev's vote
is undecided and the uncast seats can reach neither m accepts nor
n − m + 1 rejects).

evidence.description: Evidence is the evidence so far. Absent: the run's captured evidence.

report.description: Report is the progress claim. Absent: the run's data.report.

confidence.description: Confidence is the judge's confidence in Score, 0..1.

criteria.description:
Criteria carries one P(met) per judged criterion, same order as the
run's frozen acceptance (check rows are not evaluated here).

state.description:
State is judged (the judge answered), unsupported (no evidence: no call
was made), or skipped (see Reason).

would_verify.description: WouldVerify says whether this evidence would pass the verdict rule now.

accounts.description:
Accounts is the union of creator, members and every resolved group's
members: one row per account, at its highest role, saying how it is
held. Group members appear only for groups whose members.status is ok.

creator.description: Creator is null when graphs.created_by is unknown.

groups_unresolved.description:
GroupsUnresolved is true when accounts may be incomplete: a BOUND
group grant's members could not be listed for this request (members
status unavailable, forbidden, unconfigured or skipped), or v3 listed
fewer members than its total. The response is still 200; nothing is
granted or refused by it. An unbound grant, or a group v3 no longer has
(unknown_group), grants nobody and does not set it.

group_id.description:
GroupID and GroupSlug name the granted group; present for share and
group only.

kind.description:
Kind: creator (the graph's creator) | member (a legacy per-account
share) | share (a member of one of the graph's per-DAG sharing groups)
| group (a member of an ordinary granted v3 group).

Kind is accounts.kind: human, or service (an agent's identity). Absent
when v3's directory could not say (unreadable, or not in the caller's
tenant).

steward.description:
Steward is the human answerable for an agent; present only for a
service account whose agent the caller may view in v3 (AgentService).

username.description:
Username, FirstName, LastName and Email are what v3 returned for this
account in the first group's members that listed it, after v3's own
redaction, never enriched. An account no group listed (creator or legacy
member only) is filled from v3's directory under the caller's scope, by
the same rules: only for a credential that could read a v3 group member
list (unscoped or a coarse enforcer scope, never a portal link), in the
caller's tenant only, email only for a caller with tenant read. Absent
when v3 has none or the lookup failed.

via.description:
Via lists how the role is held: creator first, then a legacy member
row, then groups in groups[] order.

group_id.description:
GroupID is the stored grant's group_id, else the id resolved from v3 for
this request (never stored). Absent when neither is known.

kind.description:
Kind is "share" for one of the graph's own per-DAG sharing groups
(graph-<graph-id>-viewers|editors|admins, managed through
/graphs/{id}/members — the people the graph is shared with) and "group"
for an ordinary v3 group granted through /graphs/{id}/groups.

items.description: Items are at most 1,000 members, after v3's redaction; empty unless ok.

status.description:
Status: ok | unavailable (timeout or 5xx) | forbidden (v3 401/403) |
unknown_group (404, or the grant is bound to no group id) | unconfigured
(GRAPH_V3_BASE_URL empty) | skipped (past the 20-group cap).

total.description: Total is v3's member count; null unless status is ok.

tenant_wide_readers.description:
TenantWideReaders: accounts whose platform role reads every graph in the
tenant (TenantRead), and so see this one without any row below.

tenant_wide_writers.description:
TenantWideWriters: accounts whose platform role writes every graph in the
tenant (TenantWrite), and so are ADMIN on this one without any row below.

inherited.description:
Inherited and Shadowed appear on graph lists only: a tenant-wide row is
inherited; one a live graph-scoped profile of the same name overrides is
also shadowed.

kind.description:
Kind is agent_key (secret = an ag_ credential) or client_credentials
(client_id and client_secret of an agent-bound OAuth client).

scheme.description:
Scheme "client_credentials" makes the bridge mint a token at token_url
(client_id, client_secret, optional scope) instead of sending credentials.

eligible.description: Eligible: enough decided runs (3) for the routing fallback to use it.

rate.description: Rate is verified / (verified + rejected); null with no decided run.

type.description:
Type is the predicate. Defaults to "relates_to"; use the graph's
dependency_edge_type ("requires" by default) for scheduling edges.

Type retypes the edge (e.g. requires -> relates_to retires a stale
dependency without a delete). Omitted or equal to the current type: no
change. A real change records retyped_from / retyped_at / retyped_by in
the edge's data.

file_name.description: FileName is the SAME value given to upload-url.

role.description:
Role is the caller's own role on the folder: read | write | manage |
service, exactly as enforcer-files' folderaccess resolves it for THIS
request — never cached, never derived from the graph role alone.

complete_url.description:
CompleteURL is THIS service's public path for the second step
(POST /graphs/{id}/files/complete), never enforcer-files' in-cluster
address: PUT the bytes to upload_url, then POST {"file_name": "..."}
here under the SAME credential to record the upload.

expiry_seconds.description:
ExpirySeconds bounds the presigned URL's lifetime (enforcer-files'
default 900, max 604800). 0 uses that default.

file_name.description: FileName is the target path within the folder, e.g. "evidence/a.pdf".

overwrite.description: Overwrite allows replacing the CALLER's own existing file at that path.

assignee_group_slug.description:
AssigneeGroupSlug assigns the node to a group (contract §10); a slug,
never an account id.

links.description:
Links carries every OTHER outgoing relation, keyed by edge type — a
knowledge graph's 'cites' or 'relates_to'. Also from this node outwards,
so it cannot be inverted either.

requires.description:
Requires lists the node keys this node depends on. Reads as
"pass-1-read requires pass-0-schema".

dependency_edge_type.description:
DependencyEdgeType names the scheduling relation and defaults to
'requires'. It is what `requires:` on a node becomes.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle is "terminal" (the default: the graph completes once per
epoch) or "open" (it never completes). Anything else is 400
invalid_lifecycle.

loop.description:
Loop, when present, is set on the built graph exactly as PUT
/graphs/{graphId}/loop would set it, with the importer as set_by. A
set_by in the document is refused. on=completion with lifecycle open is
400 loop_requires_terminal.

mode.description:
Mode defaults to dag. 'graph' permits cycles, for a knowledge graph where
they are natural.

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults is the built graph's per-node-type defaults (migration
092; the shape PATCH /graphs/{graphId} takes). The document's nodes get
their type's defaults for every field they omit.

slug.description:
Slug and Name override the document's own when set, so one document can
seed a dev, a staging and a prod graph without being edited three times.

role.description:
Role is the invite's role when shared is true, else the role the caller
already held, which was at least the invite's.

shared.description:
Shared is false when the caller already held the invite's role or
higher: nothing changed, and an invite never lowers a role.

group_id.description:
GroupID is an optional ASSERTION: the v3 group the caller means. The
service resolves the slug itself and never trusts this; when both are
given and the slug now names a different group, the request is refused
with 409 group_id_mismatch instead of binding to the newcomer.

group_slug.description:
GroupSlug must name a live enforcer-v3 group in the caller's tenant, as
the caller's own credential sees it; the grant binds to that group's id.

client_policy.description:
ClientPolicy: off | warn (default) | require (migration 089). Anything
else is 400 invalid_body.

default_lease_seconds.description:
DefaultLeaseSeconds defaults to 300. 30..86400. Raise it for a graph whose
nodes are long agent runs; a node can still override it individually.

dependency_edge_type.description:
DependencyEdgeType names the edge type that expresses scheduling. The
direction is fixed: an edge reads dependent --<type>--> prerequisite.
Defaults to "requires".

description.description: Description is free prose shown in listings.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle is "terminal" (the default: the graph completes once per
epoch) or "open" (it never completes and is appended to forever).
Anything else is 400 invalid_lifecycle.

min_client_version.description:
MinClientVersion is X.Y.Z; a client below it gets client_outdated, and
under require its claim is refused.

mode.description:
Mode is "dag" (acyclicity enforced on every edge write, and topology and
frontier are available) or "graph" (cycles permitted, ordering endpoints
refuse). Defaults to "dag".

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults: per-node-type defaults (see Graph.NodeDefaults). Keys of
each entry: outputs (array), checks (array of {"check": ...} rows),
tier (mechanical|standard|deep), profile (string). Anything else is
400 invalid_body naming it.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy overrides the tenant's judgment policy for this graph:
"advisory" stores a verdict and leaves the node done; "gate" moves a
rejected node back to failed. Omitted inherits the tenant setting.

visibility.description:
Visibility "tenant" makes the graph readable by anyone in the tenant with
tenant-wide read; "private" (the default) restricts it to its creator and
explicit members.

expires_in_hours.description:
ExpiresInHours is how long the link works. Default 168 (7 days), at
most 720 (30 days).

role.description:
Role the invite shares the plan at. Default viewer, as the link works
for anyone who has it; ask for editor, which taking, finishing and
assigning work need.

status.description:
Status is active until expires_at passes (expired) or an editor
revokes it (revoked, which wins).

token.description:
Token is the secret the link carries. Shown once; send it to people,
never log it.

url.description:
URL is the portal link: GRAPH_INVITE_URL_BASE + /login#invite=<token>.
The token is in the fragment, which a browser never sends to a server.
With no base configured it is that path alone, relative to the portal.

approval.description:
Approval overrides the tenant's approval policy for this graph, key by
key (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §10). Absent means inherit.

can.description:
Can is what Role lets the caller do, from graphauth.Capabilities — the
one table GET /graphs/{id}/access also reads. Set wherever Role is.

client_policy.description:
ClientPolicy is what the graph does about a worker whose X-Graph-Client
is missing or below MinClientVersion (migration 089): off emits nothing,
warn (default) adds `warnings` to claim/heartbeat/complete responses,
require refuses the claim with 409 client_attestation_required.

default_lease_seconds.description:
DefaultLeaseSeconds is how long a claim holds a node in this graph before
another harness may take it, unless the node overrides it. A harness that
stops heartbeating within this window has its node returned to the
frontier instead of stalling the plan forever (migration 010).

effective_client_policy.description:
EffectiveClientPolicy is the policy that applies: the graph's own.
The platform never raises a graph to require; set it per graph once the
plugin ships attestation everywhere.

effective_min_client_version.description:
EffectiveMinClientVersion is the graph's own min_client_version, else the
platform default (env GRAPH_DEFAULT_MIN_CLIENT_VERSION). Set on GET only.

epoch.description: Epoch is the current epoch, 1 until the first reset (contract §2).

idle.description:
Idle is true when the graph has at least one live node and its work
roll-up (GET /graphs/{id}/summary's `state`) is complete, waiting or
stalled: nothing claimable, nothing claimed, nothing validating. A
complete terminal graph is idle; a graph-mode graph never is. Computed
on getGraph only; omitted from listGraphs.

judgment_budget.description:
JudgmentBudget bounds the judgment tokens this graph may spend
(migration 072), under the tenant's monthly cap, which still applies.
Absent means none: the graph spends the tenant's cap. Set through
PATCH /graphs/{graphId} (admin); what is left is on
GET /graphs/{graphId}/judgment/usage's budget block.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle: a terminal graph completes once per epoch; an open one never
completes (docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §1). Graphs that predate
migration 043 are terminal.

loop.description:
Loop is the graph's reset loop; null means manual resets only
(contract §4). Read-only here: it is set through the loop endpoints.

mandates.description:
Mandates are criteria appended to every run's frozen acceptance list in
this graph, after the node's own and before the tenant's (migration
040), and judged like any criterion. Absent means none.

min_client_version.description:
MinClientVersion is the oldest client version (X.Y.Z) the graph accepts
without a client_outdated warning; absent means any.

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults is how this graph's nodes are delivered, keyed by node
type (migration 092): {"task": {"outputs": [...], "checks":
[{"check": ...}], "tier": "standard", "profile": "<routing profile>"}}.
A node created without one of those fields gets its type's default
(recorded as data.node_defaults_applied); the claim card merges them at
read time for nodes that predate the default. `{}` means none.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy overrides the tenant's judgment policy for this graph
(docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §4). Absent means inherit the tenant setting.

status.description:
Status is active until expires_at passes (expired) or an editor
revokes it (revoked, which wins).

graph_name.description:
GraphName is set by the plan's editors: display text, not proof of
which plan it is.

invited_by_first_name.description:
InvitedByFirstName is the inviter's own enforcer-v3 first name. They
set it themselves, so show it quoted, as display text, never as who
they are. Absent when they have none, the directory could not be read,
or the credential could not read a v3 group member list itself (a fine
scope).

invited_by_username.description:
InvitedByUsername is the inviter's enforcer-v3 username, under the same
rules. They chose it too, but it is unique in the workspace, so no one
else can show it: it tells two people with one first name apart.

role.description: Role is the role accepting shares the plan at.

used.description:
Used is true when the caller already used this link, or an admin
shared, moved or unshared them while it was live. Accept then answers
shared false if they hold its role now, else 410 graph_invite_used:
ask for a new link rather than asking to join.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy and CreatedAt are the acting admin and the time of THIS
request on a write; on the listing they are set only for a legacy row
(v3 exposes no membership timestamp).

group_id.description: GroupID is that group's v3 id — the id gate 3 matches.

group_slug.description:
GroupSlug is the per-DAG v3 group the share is membership of. Absent
for a legacy (not yet folded) per-account row.

username.description:
Display fields exactly as enforcer-v3 returned them to the CALLER on
the listing (after v3's redaction); never stored here.

status.description:
Status is the /access vocabulary for the v3-resolved part of the
listing: ok | unavailable (timeout or 5xx; Retry-After is set) |
forbidden (v3 refused the caller's credential) | unknown_group |
unconfigured (GRAPH_V3_BASE_URL empty). Anything but ok means data
carries only the legacy per-account rows. A graph never shared is ok
with no items and makes no v3 call.

approval.description:
Approval replaces the graph's approval-policy override; its keys win
over the tenant's key by key. An explicit JSON null clears it (inherit
the tenant's); omitted leaves it. An unknown key or a value out of range
is 400 invalid_body naming the key.

client_policy.description: ClientPolicy: off | warn | require (migration 089); omitted leaves it.

judgment_budget.description:
JudgmentBudget sets the graph's judgment budget (migration 072):
monthly_tokens (required, 1..1e12) bounds the input + output tokens of
judgment attributed to this graph per UTC month, and per_epoch_tokens
(optional, 1..1e12) also bounds them per epoch. A call either would
exceed is skipped with reason graph_budget, as the tenant cap's
token_cap is. An explicit JSON null clears it; omitted leaves it; an
unknown key or a value out of range is 400 invalid_body naming the field.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle changes whether the graph ever completes: "terminal" or
"open"; anything else is 400 invalid_lifecycle. open -> terminal on a
graph whose live nodes are all done or cancelled emits graph.completed
(via lifecycle) in the same transaction; terminal -> open while the
graph has an on=completion loop is 400 loop_requires_terminal. Every
change emits graph.lifecycle_changed. Omitted leaves it.

mandates.description:
Mandates replaces the graph's mandates: at most 10, each 1..1000
characters after trimming, blank entries dropped. An explicit JSON null
(or a list with nothing left) clears them; omitted leaves them.

min_client_version.description:
MinClientVersion: X.Y.Z sets it; an explicit JSON null clears it;
omitted leaves it.

node_defaults.description:
NodeDefaults REPLACES the graph's per-type node defaults (see
Graph.NodeDefaults); `{}` or an explicit null clears them; omitted
leaves them. Existing nodes are not rewritten: the claim card merges
the defaults at read time.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy: "advisory" or "gate" sets the override; an explicit
JSON null clears it (inherit the tenant setting); omitted leaves it.

data.description:
Data is merged onto the graph's own metadata — the environment, the
service being built, whatever the caller wants to carry.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle overrides the template's: "terminal" (the default) or "open".
Anything else is 400 invalid_lifecycle; "open" on a template that
declares an on=completion loop is 400 loop_requires_terminal.

visibility.description: Visibility defaults to private, matching POST /graphs.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle and Loop are what the template or document declared
(docs/REPLAY_AND_QUERY_CONTRACT.md §1, §4); Loop is null when none.

approval.description:
Approval is the tenant's approval policy (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md
§10): how many judgment samples, how they aggregate, what is uncertain
and who is asked then. Keys absent take the defaults; a graph's own
approval overrides it key by key. Always present; `{}` is every default.

has_tenant_key.description:
HasTenantKey says whether the tenant brought its own Jev key. The key is
write-only and is never returned.

mandates.description:
Mandates are criteria appended to EVERY run's frozen acceptance list in
this tenant, after the node's own and the graph's (migration 040), and
judged like any criterion. A node author cannot remove them. Always
present; `[]` when none. Each one is a judged question on every
verification call, so ten mandates are ten more on the token meter.

monthly_token_cap.description:
MonthlyTokenCap is total (input + output) tokens per calendar month (UTC);
0 is unlimited. A call is refused when it would take usage past it.

tokens_used_this_month.description:
TokensUsedThisMonth is the sum of judgment_usage input + output tokens for the
current calendar month (UTC), the figure MonthlyTokenCap is compared to.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy is the tenant's policy as it applies to a graph with
no override of its own: the tenant's choice, or the platform default
(gate, migration 090) when the tenant never made one.

verification_policy_source.description:
VerificationPolicySource says which: `tenant` (this tenant chose it) or
`default` (no choice stored; the platform default applies, and follows
it if it ever changes).

approval.description:
Approval replaces the tenant's approval policy. Omitted (or null) keeps
it; `{}` resets every key to its default. Unknown keys and out-of-range
values are 400 invalid_body with a detail naming the key.

mandates.description:
Mandates replaces the tenant's mandates: at most 10, each 1..1000
characters after trimming; blank entries are dropped, `[]` clears them.
Omitted (or null) keeps the current list, so a client written before
mandates existed does not wipe them on every save.

model.description:
Model defaults to jev-latest and must match ^jev-. It is resolved to the
versioned id at save time and stored versioned.

tenant_key.description:
TenantKey is WRITE-ONLY. Omitted keeps the current key; the empty string
clears it (the platform key is used instead); any other value replaces
it. Stored as ciphertext; never returned, never logged.

verification_policy.description:
VerificationPolicy is the tenant's choice. Omitted or null stores no
choice: the platform default applies (gate since migration 090), so a
client that enables judgment without naming a policy gets the one
under which a rejection fails the node.

budget.description:
Budget is the graph's own judgment budget (migration 072) and what it
has spent against it: graph route only, absent when the graph has no
budget. Unlike cap it is shown to any viewer: it is the graph's
setting and the graph's spend, which this route already reports.

cap.description:
Cap is always present on the tenant route; on the graph route it is
null unless the caller holds tenant read (the tenant route's gate).

from.description: From and To are the resolved half-open window [from, to), RFC 3339 UTC.

graph_id.description: GraphID is set on the graph route only.

groups.description:
Groups: group_by=day lists every local day in the window, oldest
first, zero-filled; the other keys list keys with usage, most tokens
first, at most 500.

estimated_usd.description:
EstimatedUSD is input_tokens x estimate.price_per_mtok_usd / 1e6,
rounded to 8 decimals. An estimate, never an invoice.

graph_name.description: GraphName is the graph's name, group_by=graph only; absent for null.

key.description:
Key is the group's value: a local date YYYY-MM-DD in tz (group_by=day),
a feature, a model, a graph id or a run id. null is "not attributed":
a usage row with no graph (every row recorded before migration 068, or
a call made for no graph), or with no run (rank, align).

node_id.description: NodeID is the run's node, group_by=run only; absent for null.

resets_at.description: ResetsAt is the next 1st of the month, 00:00 UTC.

tokens_used_this_month.description:
TokensUsedThisMonth is GET /settings/judgment's tokens_used_this_month,
from the same statement: every row of the month, attributed or not.

unattributed_tokens.description:
UnattributedTokens is the part of tokens on rows with no graph (every
row recorded before migration 068 among them). Tenant route only.

external_id.description:
ExternalID is the thing's id in its own service. It may be a URL or a
name, and is never copied into activity metadata.

external_type.description: ExternalType with System names the adapter that types this link.

graph_id.description: GraphID is stamped from the node by the database; a caller never sets it.

role.description:
Role: projection (the thing mirrors this node), gate (it must be
finished before this node passes; a check names the link) or reference
(informational). A node cannot hold a projection and a gate into one
system.

evidence.description:
Evidence is what shows this fact is real: the same shape a run's evidence
takes (migration 022/023). Captured by the harness from its own tool
results, not written by hand — an assertion about an assertion is not
support. Optional: a fact with no evidence is stored and labelled
`asserted`, never refused, because a decision has no evidence to give.

source.description:
Source is free-text provenance — a document id, URL or run id — so a fact
can be traced back to what produced it.

created.description: Created is every new node, in the order given.

edges_added.description:
EdgesAdded counts every edge written: the subgraph's own, the roots'
inherited prerequisites, and the parent's new dependence on the leaves.

roots.description:
Roots inherited the parent's prerequisites; Leaves are what the parent now
requires. A single-node expansion is both.

assignee.description:
Assignee is whose work the node is (migration 043, contract §10):
present when either half is set. ADVISORY: `for=me|mine` on the
frontier and the claim narrow by it; nothing refuses a claim over it.

claimed_by.description: ClaimedBy is the running run's created_by: the account that claimed it.

lease_expires_at.description:
LeaseExpiresAt is set only while the node is running, and is the deadline
its harness must heartbeat past. Read-only: it is written by claim and
heartbeat, never set directly.

lease_seconds.description:
LeaseSeconds overrides how long a claim holds this node before another
harness may take it. NULL means the graph's default_lease_seconds.

Per node, not one constant, because the right number is not uniform: a
lease short enough to free a flaky test quickly is one that steals a
deploy out from under a live harness (migration 010).

not_before.description:
NotBefore is the time gate (migration 040): the node is neither on the
frontier nor claimable before this instant, whatever its prerequisites.
Absent when unset. A value in the past gates nothing.

opens_at.description:
OpensAt is when a time-gated node whose prerequisites are met becomes
claimable (its not_before). Set only beside not_yet_available.

rank.description:
Rank is the judged risk/effort the ranked frontier stored
(docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §9), exactly as the judge answered. It is raw
here because nodes does not compute priority — traverse does, per read —
and because migration 017's trigger clears it whenever title,
description or data change, so a value present is always about THIS
version of the node.

ready_at.description:
ReadyAt, StartedAt, EndedAt and Usage are the node's own timing and
spend (migration 088): derived facts kept by triggers, never written
by a client. See NodeUsage for why Usage is null, not zero.

reclaimable.description:
Reclaimable: the node is `running` but its lease lapsed — its harness is
presumed dead and the next claim takes it (status stays "running"; the
claim's reclaim path keys on it). Absent when false.

run_id.description: RunID is the running run, for heartbeat and completion.

runner.description:
Runner is the running run's data.runner, as the claim named it
(provenance only; absent when the claim named none).

work_state.description:
WorkState: looking_for_work (a seat is open: on the frontier, a lapsed
lease included), claimed (running under a live lease — or no lease at
all, which the nodes_running_no_lease gauge counts), looking_for_validation
(verifying: a verdict or votes pending), looking_for_arbitration
(verifying, and the latest attempt is waiting on a person),
not_yet_available (blocked on a prerequisite, or time-gated: see
opens_at), finished (done or cancelled).

assignee_account_id.description:
AssigneeAccountID assigns the node to an account (a uuid; never looked
up in v3 on write). An explicit null clears it; omitting it leaves it.

assignee_group_slug.description:
AssigneeGroupSlug assigns the node to a group by SLUG, the key group
grants use (1..255 characters, no control characters). An explicit null
clears it; omitting it leaves it. Both halves may be set together.

data.description:
Data is shallow-merged into what an existing key stores; omitting it
keeps the stored payload.

description.description: Description of an existing key is kept when omitted (or empty); a value is written.
