lease_seconds.description:
LeaseSeconds overrides the graph default for this node. 30..86400. An
upsert that omits it keeps the stored override.

not_before.description:
NotBefore gates the node until this instant (RFC 3339). An upsert that
omits it keeps the stored value; clearing it is an explicit PATCH null.

status.description:
Status of a NEW node defaults to active. On an existing key, an omitted
status keeps the node's current one; a named status is written.

title.description: Title of an existing key is kept when omitted (or empty); a value is written.

type.description:
Type of a NEW node defaults to entity. On an existing key, an omitted
(or empty) type keeps the node's stored type; a named type is written.

warnings.description: Warnings are advisory acceptance-lint findings (never an error).

archived_at.description:
Review resolution (migration 020, contract §10). ArchivedAt is set by
merge/discard (or the losing side of a contradiction pair): the row is
out of every read but never deleted. Resolution records how a curator
closed this row's review item; ResolvedContradictions lists the older
observations whose contradiction with this row has been resolved.

contradicts.description:
Contradicts lists existing observations on the same node this one
contradicts (P >= judgment.AlignContradictionMin at judgment time). Not a
foreign key: the record that a contradiction was found outlives the row.

review.description:
Review marks a judged POSSIBLE duplicate of MergedInto: stored, flagged
for a human. A row the judgment called the same fact is never stored, so
MergedInto is only ever set together with Review (migration 014 CHECK).

support.description:
Support is grounded | asserted | decision | unjudged (migration 023):
whether this fact is a measurement, a hunch, a recorded choice, or
unjudged. A LABEL, never a gate — an asserted row is stored exactly as
before. It travels on every read so a later agent can tell a hunch from a
measurement instead of treating both as established, which is the whole
point: observations are re-served as context on every claim.

candidates.description:
Candidates is how many existing observations were compared: the most
recent, at most judgment.MaxCandidates.

contradicts_weaker.description:
ContradictsWeaker is the subset of Contradicts that this observation
OUTWEIGHS: rows it disagrees with that are merely asserted, while this
one is grounded. Without it a contradiction says only "these disagree"
and a reader cannot tell which to believe — which is the whole reason
the support pair exists.

decision.description:
Decision is the alignment level, which IS the action: stored (distinct,
201), review (possible duplicate, 201 with review=true and merged_into
set), merged (the same fact, 200 with the EXISTING row and nothing
stored).

meaning.description:
Meaning spells out the contradiction in a sentence, because the ids alone
do not tell an agent what to do about them.

support.description:
Support is what this fact was judged to be: grounded (checkable and the
attached record shows it), asserted (checkable, nothing shows it),
decision (a choice or intention, with no external fact to check), or
unjudged.

judgment.description:
Judgment is present only when the add was judged, or a judgment was
attempted and could not be (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §3). Absent when
the tenant has not opted in, or the exact body dedupe answered first, so
every response that existed before judgment is byte-identical.

reason.example: auth rewrite, keep it on the deep model

tier.description:
Tier is mechanical, standard or deep; null clears the override and the
node falls back to the rules (and Jev, for a filled-in node).

assignee_account_id.description:
AssigneeAccountID assigns the node to an account (a uuid; never looked
up in v3 on write). An explicit null clears it; omitting it leaves it.

assignee_group_slug.description:
AssigneeGroupSlug assigns the node to a group by SLUG, the key group
grants use (1..255 characters, no control characters). An explicit null
clears it; omitting it leaves it. Both halves may be set together.

lease_seconds.description: LeaseSeconds sets this node's lease override. 30..86400.

not_before.description:
NotBefore gates the node until this instant (RFC 3339): it is neither on
the frontier nor claimable before then. An explicit JSON null clears it;
omitting it leaves it alone. A past value is accepted and gates nothing.
Changing it does NOT clear the node's rank (017's trigger watches only
title, description and data).

Resolution is the claim's transaction start, not the request: a value of
"now" claimed in the same second can go either way. Nothing in a plan
should depend on sub-second timing.

aggs.description:
Aggs has one entry per requested aggregate, named exactly as
requested; null when no row contributed — or, for an output
aggregate, when the contributing outputs carry different currencies
(never a sum across currencies).

currency.description:
Currency is present only when an output.<name> aggregate is requested:
the common declared currency of every contributing output, or "mixed".

key.description:
Key has one entry per group key, named as requested ("data.owner",
"created:week"); a missing value is null.

skipped.description:
Skipped counts, per jsonb-number aggregate, the rows whose value was
present but not a number and was therefore left out.

claimed_by.description: ClaimedBy is the running run's created_by: the account that claimed it.

lease_expires_at.description:
LeaseExpiresAt is set only while the node is running, and is the deadline
its harness must heartbeat past. Read-only: it is written by claim and
heartbeat, never set directly.

lease_seconds.description:
LeaseSeconds overrides how long a claim holds this node before another
harness may take it. NULL means the graph's default_lease_seconds.

Per node, not one constant, because the right number is not uniform: a
lease short enough to free a flaky test quickly is one that steals a
deploy out from under a live harness (migration 010).

not_before.description:
NotBefore is the time gate (migration 040): the node is neither on the
frontier nor claimable before this instant, whatever its prerequisites.
Absent when unset. A value in the past gates nothing.

opens_at.description:
OpensAt is when a time-gated node whose prerequisites are met becomes
claimable (its not_before). Set only beside not_yet_available.

rank.description:
Rank is the judged risk/effort the ranked frontier stored
(docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §9), exactly as the judge answered. It is raw
here because nodes does not compute priority — traverse does, per read —
and because migration 017's trigger clears it whenever title,
description or data change, so a value present is always about THIS
version of the node.

ready_at.description:
ReadyAt, StartedAt, EndedAt and Usage are the node's own timing and
spend (migration 088): derived facts kept by triggers, never written
by a client. See NodeUsage for why Usage is null, not zero.

reclaimable.description:
Reclaimable: the node is `running` but its lease lapsed — its harness is
presumed dead and the next claim takes it (status stays "running"; the
claim's reclaim path keys on it). Absent when false.

run_id.description: RunID is the running run, for heartbeat and completion.

runner.description:
Runner is the running run's data.runner, as the claim named it
(provenance only; absent when the claim named none).

work_state.description:
WorkState: looking_for_work (a seat is open: on the frontier, a lapsed
lease included), claimed (running under a live lease — or no lease at
all, which the nodes_running_no_lease gauge counts), looking_for_validation
(verifying: a verdict or votes pending), looking_for_arbitration
(verifying, and the latest attempt is waiting on a person),
not_yet_available (blocked on a prerequisite, or time-gated: see
opens_at), finished (done or cancelled).

next.description:
Next is the opaque cursor for the following page, ungrouped and
without `offset` only; pass it back unchanged as `after`. Absent on
the last page.

aggs.description:
Aggs has one entry per requested aggregate, named exactly as
requested; null when no row contributed. Duration aggregates leave
running runs out (they are still in count).

key.description:
Key has one entry per group key, named as requested ("epoch",
"started:month"); a missing value is null.

actor_client_id.description:
Attribution (migration 076, AGENTS_CONTRACT §9), stamped from the
credential that claimed the run and again from the one that completed
it when that one carried attribution. All three absent for an ordinary
credential and on runs before 076. Attribution only: nothing grants on
them; self-judgment refuses on OnBehalfOf.

ActorClientID is Tier 1: the OAuth client that acted AS created_by.

agent_id.description:
AgentID is Tier 2: the v3 agent whose credential was presented;
created_by is then that agent's service account.

client.description:
Client is the X-Graph-Client the harness sent (migration 089), e.g.
`enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Null when no request of this
run carried the header - never a fabricated value.

epoch_attempt.description:
EpochAttempt and FailedAttempts are the claim card's per-epoch numbers
(contract §5), present ONLY on the run POST .../runs just opened, so
StartRun answers what the two claim endpoints answer. Never on a list.

evidence.description:
Evidence is what the harness attached to SHOW the work happened
(§2a, migration 022). Raw so the scan list stays one line per column;
EvidenceOf decodes it. Absent on runs that attached nothing and on
every run that ended before 022.

judgment_pending_since.description:
JudgmentPendingSince is set while the run waits for the worker's Jev
call (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §12, migration 067): its verdict (the
plain path, where verification.state is `pending`), Jev's vote (a
validated run) or its typed outputs (validation with no Jev seat).
Absent once the worker wrote it, and on every run that owed no call.

on_behalf_of.description:
OnBehalfOf is the human answerable for the run: the agent's steward, or
created_by itself under an act claim.

outcome.description:
Outcome is a server-known outcome beyond status (migration 093): only
`landing_blocked` today (the work is done, its PR could not land), with
PRURL and LandingReason. Absent on every ordinary run.

outputs.description:
Outputs are the node's declared outputs as the judge decided them in
the verification call (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §2), keyed by
output name. Absent when nothing was declared or no call was made.

usage.description:
Usage is what the run spent (migration 088): null for a worker that
reported none - never coerced to zero. While the run is running it is
the harness's last heartbeat total; completion supersedes it.

validation.description:
Validation is the run's validation-v1 state (docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md
§8) when its graph had a validation config at completion: the judges
drawn, the quorum, the tally and the outcome. Absent otherwise.

verdict_resolution.description:
Verdict resolution by a curator (migration 020, contract §10): accept
keeps the verdict and stops the worker re-judging; rejudge asked for a
fresh one. Cleared whenever a new verdict is written.

verification.description:
Verification is the judgment verdict once the run ended and judgment
ran (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §2). Absent while running and on runs
that ended before judgment existed.

next.description: Next is the opaque cursor for the following page, as NodeQueryResult.

completed_at.description:
CompletedAt is when the epoch's first graph.completed was recorded; null
while incomplete and always null on an open-lifecycle graph.

current.description:
Current is true on the open epoch (ended_at is null) — the one the
graph's live nodes are in.

cycle_seconds.description: CycleSeconds is completed_at − started_at; null while incomplete.

duration_seconds.description: DurationSeconds is (ended_at, or now for the current epoch) − started_at.

ended_at.description:
EndedAt / EndedBy are set by the reset that closed this epoch; null on
the current one.

started_by.description:
StartedBy is the account that reset (for a loop, the loop's set_by; for
`created`, the graph's creator). Null when unknown.

stats.description: Stats is null on the current epoch: it is taken inside the reset.

cooldown_seconds.description:
CooldownSeconds is the wait after completion before the reset
(completion only; 0..315360000; absent means 0).

every_seconds.description:
EverySeconds is the schedule interval, counted from the epoch's start
(schedule only; 60..315360000).

force.description:
Force: whether a loop reset cancels running runs. False skips a busy
graph and retries next tick.

max_epochs.description: MaxEpochs stops the loop once epoch >= max_epochs; null is unbounded.

on.description: On is what triggers a reset: the graph completing, or a fixed interval.

expected_epoch.description:
ExpectedEpoch is the idempotency guard: when present and not the graph's
current epoch, the reset is refused 409 epoch_mismatch with detail
"epoch is N". A retry after a lost response sends the same value, gets
epoch_mismatch with N = expected + 1, and treats that as done. Omitted,
every call resets.

force.description:
Force cancels running runs (their heartbeats then answer `finished`).
False with a running run or a verifying node is 409 graph_busy.

reason.description:
Reason goes into the graph.reset event (≤ 200 runes); default "manual".
Never into graph_epochs.

epoch.description: Epoch is the new epoch every live node is now in.

from_epoch.description: FromEpoch is the epoch this reset closed.

nodes_reset.description:
NodesReset counts the live nodes moved to `active` (archived nodes are
never touched).

runs_cancelled.description:
RunsCancelled counts the running runs a forced reset closed as
`cancelled`; 0 without force.

question.description: Question is the remote agent's status message.

a2a_input.description:
A2AInput is set on an a2a_input_required item (095): the remote agent's
open question.

landing.description:
Landing is set on a landing_blocked item (093): the PR that could not
land, beside Verdict (the blocked run's, when it has one).

output.description: Output is set on an output_uncertain item.

rejections.description:
Rejections is set on a rejections_exhausted item (090), beside Verdict
(the latest rejected run's).

route.description: Route is set on a route_undecided item.

next_cursor.description: NextCursor is present when another page exists; pass it back as ?cursor=.

candidates.description:
Candidates are at most five, most probable first, each with the line
it appeared on (re-found in the run's evidence) when it can be found.

rejections.description:
Rejections is the gate rejections counted this epoch; MaxRejections
the cap in force (approval.max_rejections, graph over tenant).

archived.description: Archived lists the observation ids archived by this action.

verification_reset.description:
VerificationReset is true for rejudge: the verdict is back to unverified
and the worker will judge the run afresh.

into.description:
Into is for merge: the observation the duplicate merges into. Defaults to
the item's suspected original; must be an observation on the same node.

note.description:
Note is stored on the row written (data._review_note) and returned.
Required for override (the arbitrator's reason, stored on the run's
validation.override).

profile_id.description:
ProfileID is for approve on a route_undecided item: the agent profile
the node is routed to (method arbitrator). Required there, ignored
elsewhere.

text.description:
Text is for reply on an a2a_input_required item: the message the bridge
sends on the remote task (required there, at most 8000 characters).

reason.description:
Reason is below_threshold or tie (the arbitrator fallback), or
jev_unavailable / token_cap / budget.

why.description: Why is composed in code from the numbers, never by the model.

assigned.description: Assigned are the judges drawn for the run (accounts and group seats).

checks.description:
Checks are the verdict's evaluated {check, link} rows, so a
verdict_rejected card names the failed checks and a verdict_unverified
one the rows that could not be evaluated.

escalated.description:
Escalated is "human" on a verdict_pending item whose aggregate stayed
inside the uncertain band; PendingHuman marks one judged under
gate_human. EscalatedFallback: a claude-* escalator was asked for and
a person was asked instead.

threshold.description:
Threshold is the upheld-probability floor a criterion's noul must
reach (judgment.VerifyNoulMin); Failed lists the indexes into Criteria
of those under it.

validation.description:
Validation is set on an item for a run in validation-v1: the votes
cast and, on an escalated run, why the vote did not decide
(pool_too_small, deadline), so the arbitrator sees what they decide.

profiles_visible.description: ProfilesVisible counts enabled, live profiles a route on this graph may choose.

routing.description: Routing is the stored config with defaults applied, or null when off.

why.description: Why is composed in code from the numbers, never model text.

route.description: Route is the current row for the node's (epoch, next attempt), or null.

enabled.description:
Enabled turns routing on. Off (or no config) is byte-identical to a
graph that never had routing.

fallback.description: Fallback below the threshold or on a tie.

margin.description: Margin: the top profile must beat the runner-up by this (0..0.5, default 0.10), else it is a tie.

max_profiles.description: MaxProfiles bounds the candidates one decision weighs (1..16, default 16).

threshold.description: Threshold: Jev's top probability must reach this (0.50..0.99, default 0.65).

upstream_depth.description: UpstreamDepth is how deep the prerequisite bundle the router reads goes (1..3, default 1).

delivered.description:
Delivered says the run was still open, so the flag will actually reach a
harness on its next heartbeat. False means the run had already ended and
nothing will read this.

replayed.description:
Replayed is true when an Idempotency-Key matched an earlier claim of this
node and Data is ITS run, in its current state; nothing was claimed.
Absent on a fresh claim.

limit.description:
Limit caps how many nodes to take. Defaults to 1 and is capped at 50 —
a harness that claims the whole frontier and then dies holds every node
until something reaps it, and there is no reaper.

prefer_profiles.description:
PreferProfiles are routing-profile NAMES (at most 10). The frontier is
ordered nodes routed to one of them first, then the usual created_at, id.
It REORDERS and never FILTERS: a node routed elsewhere, or not routed, is
still claimed once the preferred ones are gone, so no node is stranded when
its preferred worker is away (docs/ROUTING_CONTRACT.md §3b).

route_override_reason.description:
RouteOverrideReason (at most 500 characters) says why the claimer runs a routed
node as something other than its route; recorded on the run as
data.route_override_reason, ignored on an unrouted node (ROUTING_CONTRACT §3b).

runner.description:
Runner is free-form provenance recorded on each run's data — a worker id,
a workflow name. It is NOT authorization and nothing reads it to decide
anything.

remaining.description:
Remaining is how many frontier nodes were left unclaimed, so a caller can
decide whether to come back immediately or wait. It is a SNAPSHOT — another
harness may take them first — and is deliberately advisory.

replayed.description:
Replayed is true when an Idempotency-Key matched an earlier claim and
these are ITS runs, in their current state; nothing was claimed. Absent
on a fresh claim.

warnings.description:
Warnings are advisories about the caller's client (migration 089):
hooks_inactive, client_outdated. Absent when there are none or the
graph's client_policy is off.

acceptance.description:
The three below are present ONLY when `include` asked for them, and are
read AFTER the claim committed, in a second transaction — so asking for
context never lengthens the row-lock window the claim holds. Pointers, not
slices, because the contract distinguishes "not asked" (absent) from
"asked, none" (`[]`): a harness that requested criteria must not have to
parse `data` to learn the node has no acceptance list.

Acceptance is `data.acceptance` surfaced typed. Skills are resolved exactly
as listNodeSkills resolves them, in load order. Observations are the
newest 20.

acceptance_evidence.description:
AcceptanceEvidence is include=criteria's third part: one `evidence` hint
per frozen row (check rows included), by row kind, so a worker knows
what the judge needs to see before it reports. VerificationPolicy is
the effective policy (graph override, else tenant): `gate` and
`gate_human` mean a rejected verdict fails the node; `advisory` does
not; `off` means nothing is judged on this tenant.

assignee.description:
Assignee is whose work the node is (contract §10), present when set.
Advisory: a claim without `for` takes assigned and unassigned alike.

data.description:
Data is the node's own payload, and it is returned here because it is
where the binding between a node and the thing that runs it lives — the
service-bootstrap template writes {"runner":"archon","workflow":"svc-schema"}.

Without it every claim needs a follow-up GET on the node just to learn what
to execute, which defeats the point of a claim returning enough to act on
and puts a second round trip in the hot loop of every harness.

epoch.description:
Epoch is the run's node_runs.epoch: the graph's epoch when the run
opened (stamped by the database, migration 043). Attempt keeps counting
across epochs; EpochAttempt does not.

epoch_attempt.description:
EpochAttempt is the 1-based count of this node's runs in this epoch,
including the one just opened. A harness's retry budget reads THIS, not
Attempt, which is monotonic across resets (contract §5).

failed_attempts.description:
FailedAttempts counts prior runs IN THIS EPOCH that failed ON THEIR
MERITS. It is NOT Attempt-1: an `abandoned` run — a harness that died and
was reclaimed — consumes an attempt number but is not evidence the work
fails. A retry budget applied to Attempt stops retrying nodes nobody ever
tried. Per epoch since replay-and-query (contract §5): identical to
before on a graph that was never reset, and 0 again after a reset.

inputs.description:
Inputs is include=inputs: each data.inputs entry resolved to an upstream
node's output in the same graph, with provenance, or `absent` with a
reason (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §4). `{}` when asked and the
node declares none, or when data.inputs is malformed (see Warnings).

last_rejection.description:
LastRejection is the verdict that sent this node back (migration 090):
the newest run of the current epoch judged `rejected`, with its
per-criterion results and reason, so the retry starts from what the
judge said rather than re-deriving it. Present on every claim (no
`include` needed) whenever such a run exists; absent otherwise.

lease_expires_at.description:
LeaseExpiresAt is the deadline this claim holds the node until. Past it,
another harness may take the node and this run is closed as `abandoned` —
so a worker that is still alive must heartbeat before then, and one that
is not stops blocking the plan (migration 010).

mandates.description:
Mandates is include=criteria's other half: the graph's and the tenant's
mandates frozen onto this run after the node's own criteria, graph then
tenant, each judged like a criterion (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md
§5). `[]` when asked and there are none. A separate field so `acceptance`
keeps its string[] type.

model.description: Model is what to launch: mechanical script-or-haiku, standard sonnet, deep opus.

not_before.description:
NotBefore is the node's time gate (migration 040), present only when
set. On a claimed node it has always passed; it is returned so a harness
sees the gate a planner put there rather than having to GET the node.

opens_at.description:
OpensAt is when a time-gated node whose prerequisites are met becomes
claimable (its not_before). Set only beside not_yet_available.

reclaimable.description:
Reclaimable: the node is `running` but its lease lapsed — its harness is
presumed dead and the next claim takes it (status stays "running"; the
claim's reclaim path keys on it). Absent when false.

reclaimed_run_id.description:
ReclaimedRunID is set when taking this node ALSO closed a dead run whose
lease had lapsed, and names the run that was abandoned. Empty in the
ordinary case. Worth surfacing: a harness that sees it knows its node was
someone else's a moment ago and any side effects of that attempt are
half-done, not absent.

route.description:
Route is the routing decision for this attempt (ROUTING_CONTRACT §3a):
ABSENT on a graph without routing, `null` when routing is on but the node
is not routed (yet), otherwise the chosen profile. Advice, not a gate.

run_status.description:
RunStatus is present ONLY on a replayed claim (Idempotency-Key): the
recorded run's status NOW — running, succeeded, failed, abandoned (it was
reclaimed) or cancelled. A fresh claim omits it; its run is `running` by
construction.

tier.description:
Tier is the EFFECTIVE tier for this attempt: the stored one, bumped one
step once an earlier attempt reached the work and failed (not a denial, not
a run with no evidence), unless a user set it.

tier_source.description: TierSource is who decided the stored tier: user, planner, rule or jev.

upstream.description:
Upstream is include=upstream: what this node's prerequisites did —
report, verdict, evidence, outputs, observations, links, file ids — as
one bounded bundle, read after the claim committed
(docs/UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md). Absent when not asked; asked with nothing
upstream it is `{"prerequisites":[], ...}`. Read fresh on a replay.

warnings.description:
Warnings name what was wrong with the node's declarations — a malformed
data.inputs today — without failing the claim: a planner's typo must not
stall the plan. Absent when there is nothing to say.

work_state.description:
WorkState: looking_for_work (a seat is open: on the frontier, a lapsed
lease included), claimed (running under a live lease — or no lease at
all, which the nodes_running_no_lease gauge counts), looking_for_validation
(verifying: a verdict or votes pending), looking_for_arbitration
(verifying, and the latest attempt is waiting on a person),
not_yet_available (blocked on a prerequisite, or time-gated: see
opens_at), finished (done or cancelled).

frontier.description:
Frontier is what became runnable once this run closed, computed in the
SAME transaction — so it reflects this outcome rather than a state that
existed before it. Under a gate policy the node is held in `verifying`
(its dependents are not in this list) and the frontier is recomputed
after the verdict moves it: to done, releasing them, or to failed.

NOT CLAIMED. Reading is deliberate: a harness that crashes between this
response and starting work would otherwise hold claims on nodes it never
began, and there is no reaper. Call /frontier/claim when actually ready.

warnings.description:
Warnings are advisories about the caller's client (migration 089);
see ClaimResponse.Warnings.

cmd.description:
command: what ran, what it exited with, what it printed.

Exit is a POINTER because it is often unknowable. A Claude Code Bash
tool_response carries no exit field: success arrives as an object
(stdout, stderr, interrupted...) and failure arrives as a plain string,
"Error: Exit code N\n<output>", which is the only place the number is
written down. A capture hook that cannot parse it must still be able to
attach the output — dropping the item would weaken the verdict in
exactly the case that matters most, a command that failed.

file.description:
File is an enforcer-files file_id holding the WHOLE of what Output
holds a clip of (adapter-files). A harness uploads a command output
longer than the clip under the user's own credential and records the id
here, so the middle the 30/70 clip elides is one click away for the
person reading the verdict. It is a uuid or it is dropped. Nothing in
this service downloads it during verification: the judge sees the clip
and a line saying the clip is not the whole (VerifyEvidenceQuestions).

file_bytes.description:
FileBytes is the stored file's size as the uploader measured it, quoted
in that line. Optional; kept only beside a file, and never negative.

kind.description:
Kind is command | file | artifact | note. An unrecognised kind is kept
and shown to the judge rather than dropped — a harness inventing a
kind is still telling us something, and silently discarding evidence
would turn a report that tried into one that did not.

path.description: file: a path and the part of it that matters.

text.description: note: prose. Accepted, and deliberately weak — see EvidenceQuestions.

criterion.description: Criterion is the row's text, or `[check] <name>` for a check row.

kind.description:
Kind is check | pr | file | prose. A row that mentions both a PR and a
file reports the first in that order; Evidence carries every hint.

mandate.description: Mandate is "graph" or "tenant" for a mandate row, else empty.

evidence.description:
Evidence is what SHOWS the work happened: up to 20 items, judged
instead of the report's claims (§2a). A succeeded run on a node with
acceptance criteria and no evidence is verified `unsupported`, never
`verified` — a claim is not evidence for itself. Over the bounds it is
clipped, never refused: a completion must not fail over an attachment.

outputs.description:
Outputs are values the harness reports for the node's declared outputs
(data.outputs), by name. Each is normalised by its declared type — one
that does not normalise, or names no declared output, is dropped with a
warning in the run's data._output_warnings — and then JUDGED against the
evidence: it is stored on the run's outputs only when the evidence shows
it (grounded >= 0.70), with source `declared`. For values that are not
verbatim in evidence, such as a computed count.

route_override_reason.description:
RouteOverrideReason (at most 500 characters): why this run departed from its
route; recorded as data.route_override_reason on a routed run, ignored otherwise.

usage.description:
Usage is what the run spent (migration 088): OPTIONAL. Omit it for a
human worker - it is then null, never zero. It supersedes any running
total a heartbeat sent; omitted here keeps the heartbeat's last.

lease_expires_at.description:
LeaseExpiresAt is the new deadline when State is ok or cancel_requested,
and zero otherwise — there is no lease to hold once the run has ended.

run_status.description:
RunStatus is the run's own status, so a caller can log what actually
happened rather than inferring it from State.

state.description: State is one of ok, cancel_requested, reclaimed, finished.

usage.description:
Usage is the run's RUNNING TOTAL so far: each heartbeat overwrites the
last, and completion supersedes it - nothing is added, so a total sent
every minute is never double counted. Omit it (or send no body) when
there is nothing to report; a human worker never does.

warnings.description:
Warnings are advisories about the caller's client (migration 089); see
ClaimResponse.Warnings. Only on a run that is still running.

epoch.description:
Epoch is the run's epoch: the graph's current one, or an earlier one
only when the reference said `@previous`.

pr_url.description: PRURL is the pull request that could not land (http or https).

reason.description: Reason says why it is blocked (up to 2000 characters).

rejections.description:
Rejections is the gate rejections counted toward the cap this epoch
(graph_node_rejections); MaxRejections is the cap in force
(approval.max_rejections, graph over tenant, default 3). When the next
rejection makes them equal, the node needs review instead of failing.

verification.description:
Verification is that run's verdict as stored: state rejected, the
reason (unsupported_by_evidence, check_failed, rejected_by_human ...),
one P(met) per criterion and the failed checks.

actor_client_id.description:
Attribution (migration 076, AGENTS_CONTRACT §9), stamped from the
credential that claimed the run and again from the one that completed
it when that one carried attribution. All three absent for an ordinary
credential and on runs before 076. Attribution only: nothing grants on
them; self-judgment refuses on OnBehalfOf.

ActorClientID is Tier 1: the OAuth client that acted AS created_by.

agent_id.description:
AgentID is Tier 2: the v3 agent whose credential was presented;
created_by is then that agent's service account.

client.description:
Client is the X-Graph-Client the harness sent (migration 089), e.g.
`enforcer-graph-plugin/0.14.0; hooks=on`. Null when no request of this
run carried the header - never a fabricated value.

epoch.description: the graph's epoch when the run opened (043); attempt counts across epochs

epoch_attempt.description:
EpochAttempt and FailedAttempts are the claim card's per-epoch numbers
(contract §5), present ONLY on the run POST .../runs just opened, so
StartRun answers what the two claim endpoints answer. Never on a list.

evidence.description:
Evidence is what the harness attached to SHOW the work happened
(§2a, migration 022). Raw so the scan list stays one line per column;
EvidenceOf decodes it. Absent on runs that attached nothing and on
every run that ended before 022.

judgment_pending_since.description:
JudgmentPendingSince is set while the run waits for the worker's Jev
call (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §12, migration 067): its verdict (the
plain path, where verification.state is `pending`), Jev's vote (a
validated run) or its typed outputs (validation with no Jev seat).
Absent once the worker wrote it, and on every run that owed no call.

on_behalf_of.description:
OnBehalfOf is the human answerable for the run: the agent's steward, or
created_by itself under an act claim.

outcome.description:
Outcome is a server-known outcome beyond status (migration 093): only
`landing_blocked` today (the work is done, its PR could not land), with
PRURL and LandingReason. Absent on every ordinary run.

outputs.description:
Outputs are the node's declared outputs as the judge decided them in
the verification call (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §2), keyed by
output name. Absent when nothing was declared or no call was made.

usage.description:
Usage is what the run spent (migration 088): null for a worker that
reported none - never coerced to zero. While the run is running it is
the harness's last heartbeat total; completion supersedes it.

validation.description:
Validation is the run's validation-v1 state (docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md
§8) when its graph had a validation config at completion: the judges
drawn, the quorum, the tally and the outcome. Absent otherwise.

verdict_resolution.description:
Verdict resolution by a curator (migration 020, contract §10): accept
keeps the verdict and stops the worker re-judging; rejudge asked for a
fresh one. Cleared whenever a new verdict is written.

verification.description:
Verification is the judgment verdict once the run ended and judgment
ran (docs/JUDGMENT_CONTRACT.md §2). Absent while running and on runs
that ended before judgment existed.

warnings.description: Warnings are advisories about the caller's client (migration 089).

node_moved.description:
NodeMoved: this verdict moved the node to `failed`. A gating rejection
of an attempt that was already superseded records false.

state.description:
State repeats verification.state so a list can be scanned without
opening each verdict.

data.description:
Data is free-form attempt context — a transcript reference, a model id, a
token budget.

source.description:
Source: reported (the provider's own counters) or estimated (the
harness's guess). Defaults to reported when omitted.

confidence.description:
Confidence is snowball's consecutive-round count for the outcome it
stopped on (snowball only; >= beta when decided). Not the judge's
confidence, which is the verdict's own `confidence`.

decided.description:
Decided: snowball reached beta consecutive agreeing rounds (snowball
only). False means max_rounds passed undecided: the criteria and score
are the median of every sample and the verdict was escalated per
escalate_to. When true they are the median of the samples whose
outcome was the decision.

n.description:
N is how many samples came back; fewer than asked when a resample
failed or the tenant's token cap refused it.

rounds.description: Rounds is how many snowball rounds were drawn (snowball only).

aggregate.description:
Aggregate says how the verdict's criteria and score were combined.
Present on every verdict the judge answered.

attempts.description:
Attempts is how many times this run has been judged; the re-judge
worker increments it.

checks.description:
Checks is one result per {check, link} row of the frozen list, in
frozen order (docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §8). Evaluated in code
before any judgment call; absent when the list has no check rows.

criteria.description:
Criteria carries one P(met) per data.acceptance entry, same order. On
the evidence path this is P(the evidence SHOWS it), not P(the report
claims it).

criteria_changed.description:
CriteriaChanged: the node's acceptance criteria were edited after this
run was claimed. The verdict is on the criteria frozen at claim
(migration 031) — the ones the worker was given — and this says the
node now asks for something else, so a reader knows to look.

decided_by.description:
DecidedBy: quorum when validation-v1's judges decided this verdict,
arbitrator when a person resolved its escalation. Absent on a judge's
verdict.

escalated.description:
Escalated is "human" when the aggregate was still inside the uncertain
band and the policy's escalate_to handed it to a person: the verdict
waits as a verdict_pending review item, and a verifying node stays
verifying until it is approved or rejected.

escalated_fallback.description:
EscalatedFallback: escalate_to named an escalator this service does not
have (claude-*), and a person was asked instead.

evidenced.description:
Evidenced records which question was asked. false means the verdict is
about the report's claims — the pre-022 behaviour, kept only for runs
whose harness attached nothing and which are judged anyway.

low_confidence.description:
LowConfidence: a gate rejection whose confidence was below
approval.min_reject_confidence (migration 091). The node was NOT failed:
it stays verifying and a low_confidence_rejection review item waits for
a person. It does not count toward max_rejections unless the person
then rejects it.

model.description: Model is the versioned id the service reported, never the alias.

pending_human.description:
PendingHuman: judged under gate_human, so the verdict waits for a
person however it came out; the node stays verifying.

policy.description:
Policy is the policy in force when judged; absent when skipped.
`validation` marks a verdict validation-v1 wrote: a quorum decision
(decided_by quorum), or an escalation (escalated human, reason
pool_too_small or deadline) waiting for an arbitrator.

question_hash.description:
QuestionHash is the sha256 of exactly what the judge was asked (state
and questions). Present only when a call was made. Two verdicts on one
run with different hashes were judged on different criteria or evidence
(migration 032 keeps every verdict in run_verdicts).

reason.description:
Reason is present only when unverified (`unavailable`, `key_unusable`,
`write_failed`, `check_error`), rejected by a check (`check_failed`),
unsupported
(`no_evidence`), rejected on the evidence path
(`unsupported_by_evidence`), or skipped (`judgment_disabled`,
`no_acceptance`, `not_succeeded`, `token_cap`).

resolved_by_human.description:
ResolvedByHuman: a person approved or rejected this verdict from the
review queue.

restates.description:
Restates is the evidence path's veto: P(the evidence is the claim in
other words). Present only when the evidence path ran.

samples.description:
Samples is one entry per verification call the aggregate is over, the
first first, present only when there was more than one (approval
policy, docs/OUTPUTS_AND_LINKS_CONTRACT.md §10). Each is also a
run_verdicts row with applied = false.

score.description: Score is the overall three-level score in [0,2]; Confidence in [0,1].

state.description:
State `pending` (067) is not a verdict: the run is waiting for the
worker's Jev call, and every other field but policy, checks,
criteria_changed, judged_at (when it became pending) and attempts (0) is
absent. The verdict replaces it; GET the run, or complete with
?wait=judgment during the transition period (JUDGMENT_CONTRACT §12).

message.example: no X-Graph-Client header: heartbeats, evidence and usage are not being captured

reason.description: Reason is the text after `hooks=off:` when the client gave one.

node_types.description:
NodeTypes limits the skill to nodes of these types; omitted or null means
every type. An empty list is 400 invalid_body (it would match nothing).

pin_version.description:
PinVersion pins this attachment to a specific version. Omit to follow the
latest.

position.description:
Position omitted means APPEND. It never means 0 — see the note on the
insert below.

pinned_version.description:
PinnedVersion nil means "follow the latest published version". A value
pins, which is what makes a graph an agent walks reproducible instead of
drifting when someone publishes a new version underneath it.

position.description:
Position is the load order and is therefore part of the contract, not
decoration.

source.description:
Source says where the attachment came from on a node's resolved list:
"graph" (a graph-level skill matching the node's type, migration 092)
or "node" (attached to this node). Graph-level skills load first.

body.example: # Verify loop -- run build, vet and tests before calling anything done.

description.example: Run build, vet and tests before calling anything done.

node_types.description: NodeTypes filters which nodes the skill applies to; null means every type.

description.description:
Description is how an agent decides whether to load the body at all, so it
is required rather than optional.
description.example: Run build, vet and tests before calling anything done.

center.description: Center restricts the export to a node's neighbourhood.

file_name.description:
FileName overrides the derived name. The extension is chosen from the
format when omitted.

format.description: Format is mermaid, markdown, text or dot.

content.description:
Content is the rendered text, returned alongside the stored file so a
caller gets the export in the same round trip that persists it.

waiting.description:
Waiting lists nodes that would be in Data but for a not_before still in
the future (prerequisites satisfied, claimable status, not archived),
earliest first, at most 200. Always present; `[]` when none. An empty
Data with a non-empty Waiting means "not yet", not "blocked".

assignee.description: Assignee is whose work the node is (contract §10), present when set.

depth.description:
Depth is the hop distance from the centre, and is only set by the
neighborhood endpoint.

not_before.description:
NotBefore is the node's time gate, set only by the frontier endpoint and
only when the node has one. On a frontier node it has always passed.

opens_at.description:
OpensAt is when a time-gated node whose prerequisites are met becomes
claimable (its not_before). Set only beside not_yet_available.

rank.description: Rank is set only by the frontier endpoint with rank=1 (contract §9).

reclaimable.description:
Reclaimable: the node is `running` but its lease lapsed — its harness is
presumed dead and the next claim takes it (status stays "running"; the
claim's reclaim path keys on it). Absent when false.

work_state.description:
WorkState: looking_for_work (a seat is open: on the frontier, a lapsed
lease included), claimed (running under a live lease — or no lease at
all, which the nodes_running_no_lease gauge counts), looking_for_validation
(verifying: a verdict or votes pending), looking_for_arbitration
(verifying, and the latest attempt is waiting on a person),
not_yet_available (blocked on a prerequisite, or time-gated: see
opens_at), finished (done or cancelled).

stale.description:
Stale is true when risk/effort are null for a reason other than judgment
being off: over the batch bound or the judge unavailable. A stored rank
that predates a node change is never served — the 017 trigger clears it.

data.description:
Data is in execution order: ascending level, which is the REVERSE
topological order of the dependency edges themselves.

depth.description: Depth is the depth that was applied.

edge_type.description: EdgeType is the graph's dependency_edge_type: the one relation walked.

prerequisites.description:
Prerequisites are ordered by distance, then key. Archived nodes and the
node itself never appear.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when prerequisites were left out for the bundle's
byte ceiling (MaxBundleBytes) or its count ceiling (MaxPrerequisites).

distance.description: Distance is the fewest hops from the node the bundle is for.

files.description: Files are enforcer-files ids this prerequisite points at, ids only.

links.description: Links are the node's links, oldest first, at most MaxLinks.

observations.description: Observations are the newest MaxObservations, newest first.

outputs.description:
Outputs are the outputs of the run in Run, present values only; `{}`
when there is no run or it has none. The run is their provenance.

run.description:
Run is the highest-attempt succeeded run of this node in the graph's
CURRENT epoch, or null — a prior epoch's run is never shown.

status.description:
Status is the node's status as of the read. Only distance-1
prerequisites are guaranteed finished (done or cancelled).

truncated.description:
Truncated is whether a section cap or the byte budget cut anything;
Truncation names the sections, in the order they were first cut.

evidence.description: Evidence is what the judge saw (NormaliseEvidence), then tighter.

report.description:
Report is data.report, head-and-tail clipped; absent when data has no
report (never the whole data object).

verdict.description: Verdict is the run's verification decision; null when never judged.

validation.description: Validation is node_runs.validation.state when the run was validated.

previous_judges.description:
PreviousJudges are the first vote's judges (and "jev" when Jev sat):
none of them holds a seat in the re-opened vote.

previous_tally.description: PreviousTally is the first vote's tally.

rejected_at.description: RejectedAt is when the appealed rejection was decided.

note.description:
Note says why the rejection is wrong; stored on the appeal (at most
4000 characters).
Note is the judge's reason, stored on the vote (at most 4000 characters).
note.example: the evidence shows the migration ran

arbitrators.description:
Arbitrators are explicit grants IN ADDITION to the graph owner and
tenant admins, who always arbitrate.

deadline_seconds.description:
DeadlineSeconds: a run still undecided this long after it entered
validation escalates (reason `deadline`). 60..2592000; absent means
86400.

jev.description:
Jev: Jev is one of the n judges, its vote the graph's approval
policy's aggregate (accept, reject, or undecided inside the band).

reason.description:
Reason is why the last attempt cast nothing: unavailable, key_unusable,
token_cap, check_error.

verdict_id.description:
VerdictID is the run_verdicts row (applied = false) holding Jev's
aggregate — the approval policy's verdict this vote was read from.

vote.description: Vote is accept, reject or undecided; absent while uncast.

groups.description:
Groups are v3 group SLUGS naming live groups in the caller's tenant.
Each is BOUND to its v3 group id when the config is written (063), and
is one seat in the draw, filled by whichever member of THAT group (by
id) votes first — never by a later group that took the slug.

scope.description:
Scope: private (owner + accounts/groups), workspace (owner + graph
members + accounts/groups; the graph must be tenant-visible),
allowlist (only accounts/groups; at least one), none (no people;
Jev alone: requires jev and n = 1).

from.description: From is the quorum's decision the arbitrator overturned.

m.description: M: how many must agree. ceil(n/2) <= m <= n, so a minority never decides.

n.description: N: judges assigned to each run. 1..15.

appeal.description:
Appeal is set once the run's producer appealed a rejection (§6a): the
vote was re-opened with fresh seats, excluding PreviousJudges.

assigned.description:
Assigned are the judges drawn at random for this run: account ids and
"group:<slug>" seats (any member of that group may fill one).

config.description:
Config is the graph's config AS IT WAS when this run entered
validation: editing the graph's config never changes a vote in flight.

deadline_at.description:
DeadlineAt is when a still-pending run escalates for `deadline`:
opened_at + config.deadline_seconds. Computed, never stored (045's
validation_deadline_at is the stored rule).

decided_by.description:
DecidedBy is quorum on a vote's decision, arbitrator once an escalated
run was approved or rejected; null while pending or escalated.

escalated_at.description: EscalatedAt is when the run escalated; absent otherwise.

filled.description:
Filled maps each seat that has voted to the account that filled it,
so one group seat is filled once.

jev.description:
Jev is Jev's seat, present once Jev was asked: the vote it cast (or
the attempts that could not cast one). Absent when jev is false.

override.description:
Override is set once an arbitrator overturned the quorum's decision
(§6a): who, when, the note and the decision overturned. DecidedBy is
then arbitrator.

reason.description:
Reason is set when escalated: pool_too_small (fewer eligible judges
than n when validation opened), deadline, or jev_undecided (Jev's vote
is undecided and the uncast seats can reach neither m accepts nor
n − m + 1 rejects).

voter.description:
Voter is the account that voted (never a group seat), or "jev". An
undecided Jev casts no row: see the run's validation.jev.

node_ids.description:
NodeIDs is one such chain in PATH ORDER (graph_remaining_critical_path_v2,
073): the root first — unfinished, every prerequisite met, the next thing
to do — each later id a dependent of the one before it (archived nodes
are transparent and never listed), the far end last. Always exactly
Remaining long: when Bounded, the first 1000 nodes of a longer chain.
Ties between equally long chains go to the lowest node key. Empty, never
null, when nothing remains.

by_type.description:
ByType, BySkill, ByGroup break the open work seats down so a worker can
self-select. ByGroup is the assignee group slug, with `nobody` for an
unassigned node (a node assigned to an account only is in neither).

judges_wanted.description:
JudgesWanted is open judge seats: assigned, not yet filled, Jev's
excluded, on pending validations.

opens_next_at.description: OpensNextAt is the earliest opens_at among not_yet_available nodes.

workers_wanted.description:
WorkersWanted is min(frontier_size, max_parallel − live leases) when
max_parallel is set, else frontier_size. ADVISORY: nothing refuses a
claim over it.

audience_without_claim.description:
AudienceWithoutClaim (PUT only) names every listed account and
"group:<slug>" whose role on the graph would NOT carry claim: the
advert reaches them, the claim will not. Grant them editor (a member or
group grant) if they should work the plan.

groups_unresolved.description:
GroupsUnresolved (PUT only) is true when the graph has group grants
whose members v3 could not list for this request (v3 unreachable, no
service key, or more than 16 granted groups): a listed account that is
an editor only through a group may then be named in
audience_without_claim although it can claim. The warning errs toward
naming; nothing is granted or refused by it.

input_tokens.description: Token and cost totals are null (omitted) when no run reported any.

runs_by_client.description:
RunsByClient counts the graph's runs (every epoch) by the X-Graph-Client
they reported (migration 089); RunsWithoutClient counts the runs that
reported none (a harness running without the plugin's hooks). The two
add up to every run of the graph.

verdicts.description: Verdicts counts judged runs by verification state, this epoch and overall.

claim.description:
Claim and Validations are where to act: the existing atomic claim and
the caller's assigned validations. The lobby never reserves a seat.

my_role.description:
MyRole and MyCan are the caller's role on the graph and what it
carries (graphauth.Capabilities), so a worker sees BEFORE claiming
whether it holds `claim`. A row with work seats and no claim is the
honest shape of "advertised to you, not granted to you": the audience
advertises only.

opens_next_at.description:
OpensNextAt is the graph's earliest opens_at (a time-gated node whose
prerequisites are met), unfiltered.

state.description: State is the graph's roll-up (as getGraphSummary's), unfiltered.

workers_wanted.description:
WorkersWanted is the counted work seats, capped by the graph's advisory
max_parallel less its live leases.

run_seconds.description:
RunSeconds is the sum of this epoch's run durations (a running run
counts to now). Absent when the node has no run this epoch.

usage.description:
Usage is the node's rollup; absent when it has no runs. Totals inside
are null, not 0, when no run reported usage.

wait_seconds.description:
WaitSeconds is ready_at to started_at: how long runnable work sat
unclaimed. Absent until the node has started. Never negative (a node
can start before a later re-stamp of its ready_at).

audience.description:
Audience: private (owner and tenant admins, plus accounts/groups),
workspace (anyone in the tenant who can see the graph; the graph must be
tenant-visible), allowlist (only accounts/groups; at least one). The
words validation's judges.scope uses, minus none.

groups.description: Groups are v3 group SLUGS (at most 100).

max_parallel.description:
MaxParallel caps workers_wanted at max_parallel − live leases
(1..10000, or null for no cap). ADVISORY: nothing refuses a claim at
the cap; it only shapes what the lobby asks for.

open.description:
Open false keeps the config but withdraws the advert: the lobby skips
the graph, GET still shows it. DELETE forgets the audience.

priority.description: Priority is the lobby's tie-break after demand, 0..100 (default 50).

by_status.description: ByStatus carries every node_status value, zero when absent.

complete.description: Complete is graph_is_complete: always false for an open graph.

idle.description: Idle is getGraph's idle: state is complete, waiting or stalled.

state.description:
State is the roll-up: complete (terminal and every live node finished),
recruiting (a work or judge seat is open), working (nothing open, but a
run or a verdict is in flight), waiting (on the clock, or an open graph
with nothing unfinished) or stalled (unfinished work nothing can reach —
the one that alerts).

usage.description: Usage is what the graph has spent so far (see SummaryUsage).

verdicts.description: Verdicts counts judged runs by verification state, this epoch and overall.

cache_read_input_tokens.description:
CacheReadInputTokens and CacheCreationInputTokens are null when no run
reported them; ByModel is empty, never null.

median_duration_seconds_24h.description:
MedianDurationSeconds24h over the last day's succeeded runs; null when
there were none.

escalated.description: Escalated is looking_for_arbitration: a person must decide.
